a, Correspondence between the GB cell-state annotations used in this study and the GB meta-modules defined by Neftel et al.10. Each malignant cell was scored for every Neftel meta-module by signature scoring on log-normalized RNA (excluding the cell-cycle modules G1/S and G2/M), and assigned to its highest-scoring module. Shown is the proportion of cells in each cell state that map to each Neftel et al. meta-module. b, Cell-state prediction accuracy of the classifier in Fig. 1b, trained on gene expression from a random 80% of 16,423 metacells (9,464 GB, 6,959 TME; 12 patients). Accuracy is shown for the held-out 20% (n = 3,285) using gene expression, and for all metacells using gene accessibility. Cell states are predicted less accurately from accessibility than from expression, most pronounced for malignant states, indicating elevated epigenetic plasticity. c, Uncertainty (entropy) of expression-based cell-state predictions per metacell (n = 16,423 metacells). Low uncertainty across all cell states confirms that expression profiles support confident state assignment. d, Evaluation of cell-state prediction accuracy of the cell-state classifier as in b, however trained on human neurodevelopmental cell types of a multi-ome brain atlas (12 donors; early fetal, late fetal and post-natal stages48), evaluated based on gene expression (held-out 20%; n = 512 metacells) and gene accessibility (n = 2,559 metacells). Cell-state predictions show comparable accuracy across modalities, except in progenitor populations. e, Epigenetic plasticity across neurodevelopmental metacells (n = 2,559), analysed as in Fig. 1c,d. Top: Epigenetic plasticity score (prediction entropy) across the cell types in d. Bottom: Percentage of cells from each expression-defined state (columns) assigned to each state from gene accessibility (rows). Off-diagonal values reflect accessibility compatible with several transcriptional states. As expected, radial glia and NPCs show the highest epigenetic plasticity (P = 7.5 × 10−59, two-sided t-test). f, Schematic of the canonical neurodevelopmental lineage relationships among the cell types analysed in d,e. Radial glia sit at the apex and give rise to three differentiation routes: Towards neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes, with plasticity decreasing along each route as cells mature. g, Global correlation between gene expression and accessibility in GB metacells (Pearson r across n = 21,369 genes), stratified by cell state. The concordance of correlation levels across GB cell states suggests that state-specific differences in epigenetic plasticity are not driven by differences in the global coupling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility. h, Average epigenetic plasticity per patient (n = 12) for the cell states in b, computed with the linear model of Fig. 1e after downsampling each state to equal cell numbers. Plasticity trends match those in Fig. 1e, indicating that the observed differences are not driven by variation in cell abundance. i, Average epigenetic plasticity score of GB states (n = 9) across patients. Although individual patients exhibit variation in plasticity across states, the average plasticity is comparable across patients (one-way ANOVA, P = 0.53). j, Donor-associated variation in epigenetic plasticity within defined cell neighbourhoods, shown as the ratio of the standard deviation of mean plasticity scores across donors to the standard deviation across all cells. Values were computed using k = 10 or k = 30 neighbours for each metacell (n = 4,813 and n = 11,868 metacells respectively), considering neighbourhoods represented by at least three donors, and stratified by state. Donor-associated variation was lower than overall local variation in plasticity across all malignant states. Box plots in c,e,g–j show median and IQR, 1.5 × IQR (whiskers), and outliers. Illustration in f created in BioRender; Mall, M. https://biorender.com/51tfsoq (2026).

a, Two-phase training scheme. Phase 1: Topic construction by joint training of the core autoencoder modules. scDORI embeds paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq profiles in a shared latent Topic space, from which three modules reconstruct the data. Module 1 maps Topic proportions to peak accessibility through a linear decoder with batch-specific adjustments. Module 2 predicts gene expression from the denoised Topic-specific accessibility of Module 1, using a learnable gene–peak linkage matrix restricted to a fixed genomic window around each gene. Module 3 reconstructs TF expression through Topic-TF weights. The three modules are trained jointly, minimizing the sum of their reconstruction losses together with regularization terms. Phase 2: Fine-tuning for eGRN inference. A fourth module infers Topic-specific TF–gene-regulatory links. In silico TF–peak binding scores, signed for activation or repression, are weighted by Topic-specific peak accessibility (Module 1) and propagated to target genes through the gene–peak links (Module 2). Learnable TF–gene-Topic weights adjust these links according to TF–target expression co-variation, and activating and repressive contributions are combined into a net regulatory score that predicts gene expression from Topic-level TF expression (Module 3). The encoder, gene–peak links, and Topic–peak decoder are optionally frozen during fine-tuning, with sparsity constraints on the learned TF–gene weights. b, Training runtime of scDORI as a function of dataset size, shown for Phase 1, Phase 2, and both phases combined, measured on subsampled multi-ome data from the GB atlas. Runtime scales to datasets of millions of cells. Empirical runtimes on a single NVIDIA V100 GPU (32 GB). c, Assessment of peak–gene link predictions in three cell lines (IMR90, K562, GM12878) of the published ENCODE dataset76,77, converted to semi-synthetic single-cell multi-ome data as in18 and scored against curated experimentally supported enhancer–gene links from BENGI33 as ground truth. Benchmarks span nine evidence x cell-line combinations available in BENGI, drawn from seven evidence sources derived from chromatin configuration, perturbation, and genomic interaction assays. AUPRC is shown for recovered peak–gene pairs with scDORI and SCENIC+. scDORI achieved higher AUPRC than SCENIC+ in all nine comparisons (P = 2.0 × 10−3, one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, n = 9 paired comparisons). Illustration in a created in BioRender; Mall, M. https://biorender.com/51tfsoq (2026).

a, Average Topic activity in malignant and TME states. Extended version of Fig. 2c showing data for 31 Topics (all Topics with max activation > 0.1 across cells). Key biological functions of each Topic based on GSEA are shown. Raw values and complete pathway analysis are reported in Supplementary Table 2. b, Activity of GB-associated Topics in all cells visualized on the UMAP representation of Fig. 1a. State-specific, inter-state, and pan-state Topics are labelled accordingly. c, Activity of GB-associated Topics across patients. Shown is the number of patients with at least 1% of their cells exhibiting activity (>0.05) for each Topic. All GB Topics are active in at least 4 out of 12 patients, confirming that Topics capture universal regulatory programs of GB.

a, UMAP visualization of ATAC peaks in the patient atlas using Topic–peak scores (from scDORI Module 1) as embedding. (Left) Z-scored accessibility of peaks in each GB state. (Right) Topic–peak score for selected Topics. Topics identify distinct groups of co-accessible peaks within each GB state, reflecting different gene-regulatory programs active in those states. b, Genomic distance distributions between peak–gene pairs inferred by scDORI or MOFA29. For each peak in a MOFA factor, we picked the closest gene that was also part of the same factor. Red lines mark the cis-distance (150 kb) constraint applied to scDORI. Black lines indicate the ±1 Mb assessment window, and interchromosomal peak–gene pairs are shown separately on the left. c, Comparison of cell type prediction in our GB dataset using three latent space embeddings: scDORI (50 Topics), MOFA (50 factors), and SCENIC+ (AUCell-based TF activity scores from 195 TFs). Logistic regression models were trained to predict cell type labels from the latent embeddings of each method, using n = 9,464 GB and n = 6,959 TME metacells as input. scDORI achieved higher mean per-cell type accuracy (88.0%) than MOFA (80.3%; 17/17 cell types, P = 8 × 10−6) and SCENIC+ (85.2%; 11/17 cell types, P = 2.7 × 10−3), with the advantage over SCENIC+ concentrated in malignant states. P-values were obtained from a one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test. d, Stability of scDORI gene programs across random initializations. Shown is the Jaccard similarity between the top 500 genes of the most active Topic in each GB state, comparing the reference run (Run 0) against three additional runs trained with different random seeds. A randomized version of the reference Topic–gene set serves as a negative control. Gene programs are recovered consistently across runs. e, Activity patterns of selected scDORI Topics derived from our patient atlas projected onto a reference single-cell GB atlas from Neftel et al.10. Colour denotes average Topic activity, and bars on the left show the proportion of cells from each state in our atlas among the top 5,000 cells for each scDORI Topic. The mapping of scDORI Topics to GB cell states is highly concordant across datasets. f, Activity of selected scDORI Topics within malignant cells of the Neftel GB atlas in e, visualized on a UMAP embedding. Neftel state annotations and Leiden-clustered subpopulations are indicated. g, Performance of scDORI and SCENIC+ eGRNs in predicting DEGs between the Neftel GB cell states shown in e, following the GRaNPA21 framework. For each state pair a logistic regression model was trained to predict whether each gene is up- or downregulated based on the signed TF–gene links in each eGRN. Genes were split into four cross-validation folds, with test genes held out from training. AUPRC is shown for all state pairs. Centre line, mean; error bars, s.d. Both methods outperform randomized control eGRNs (P = 3.1 × 10−5 for each, one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, n = 15 pairs) and perform comparably to each other. h, Performance of scDORI and SCENIC+ in predicting DEGs between the Leiden clusters shown in f, computed as in g. AUPRC is shown for every cluster pair, considering either scDORI or SCENIC+ eGRNs. Centre line, mean; error bars, s.d. Both methods outperform randomized control eGRNs (P = 4.4 × 10−19 and P = 4.3 × 10−19, respectively; one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, n = 104 pairs).

a, Quality control of the gain-of-function screen described in Fig. 3. Shown are distributions of UMI counts, detected genes, and mitochondrial read fractions, stratified by seeding density (High: 14,000 cells/cm2; low: 9,000 cells/cm2) and biological replicate, separately for each PDGC line (S24, P3XX, and BG5). b, Cells recovered after quality control and barcode demultiplexing. Left: Relative contribution of each cell line, replicate, and seeding density to the total of 261,566 cells. Right: Fraction of cells recovered per TF perturbation, shown for the pooled dataset and for each patient line. TF representation is balanced across lines. n = 3 (BG5) and n = 6 (S24, P3XX). c, Expression bimodality coefficients (BC) of all screened TFs in OE and control cells from b. Each dot is a TF (n = 55). Violin centre line, median; error bars, extrema. Expression is bimodal (BC > 0.555) for every TF in the OE populations and for 54 of 55 TFs in the controls, reflecting heterogeneous expression of the targeted TFs and motivating exclusion of low- and high TF-expressing cells from respective populations in each OE-versus-control comparison. Inset: ASCL1 expression in control and ASCL1-overexpressing cells. d, Effect of the endogenous-expression filter on control cell heterogeneity in b. Each dot is one TF from the OE screen (n = 55), showing the change in state proportions (left) or in average entropy (right) after removing control cells with high endogenous expression of that TF (above the tenth percentile). Centre line, mean; error bars, s.d. Filtering left state heterogeneity essentially unchanged: change in entropy did not differ from zero (P = 0.14, two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, n = 220) and mean changes in individual state proportions were at most 0.025. e, Proportion of cells from each GB state in unperturbed control populations across pooled or individual PDGC lines in b. Total cell counts per condition indicated above. All GB states are, to varying degrees, represented in control cells across all lines. f, Validation of state regulator ranking by scDORI and SCENIC+. For each GB state, the average change in state probability (Δ state score, OE versus control) is shown for the top N predicted regulators of that state, with the average change in the remaining TFs (54 − N) plotted below for comparison. Shaded regions indicate s.d. intervals. Regulators nominated by scDORI induced their predicted state more strongly than those nominated by SCENIC+ (P = 8.2 × 10−10, one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, n = 40 state × N combinations, scDORI higher in 34 of 40), most notably for the neuronal-like and AC-like states. g, Induction of Topic programs after gain-of-function of scDORI-predicted regulators of each Topic. For each top regulator (scDORI regulator score > 0.25), the change in activity of its predicted Topic is shown (Δ Topic score, OE vs. control). Dot size denotes the number of PDGC lines in which the effect was significant (label-permutation test, Benjamini–Hochberg FDR < 0.05) and colour denotes the scDORI regulator score. Regulators of nearly all Topics induced their predicted Topic program. All Topic-level effects per TF are provided in Supplementary Table 3. h, Concordance of Topic- and state-level effects after OE of scDORI-predicted regulators. Each point corresponds to one TF-Topic prediction, positioned by the change it induced in that Topic (x-axis) and in the corresponding state (y-axis), relative to control cells. TFs predicted to regulate several Topics appear once per Topic. Colour denotes the predicted Topic and dot style the significance category (label-permutation test, Benjamini–Hochberg FDR < 0.05). Most regulators induced Topic and state changes consistent with scDORI predictions (Supplementary Table 3). i, Number of DEGs per TF OE condition versus the number of OE cells, per cell line in b. The dashed line depicts a linear regression fit. DEG count scaled positively with the number of OE cells (Spearman r = 0.87, P = 1.9 × 10−50, n = 162 TF × cell-line conditions), reflecting increased statistical power with greater cell coverage. j, Number of upregulated and downregulated genes in TF-overexpressing cells relative to control cells in each PDGC line in b. Bars show the mean ± s.d. of each direction. n = 3 (BG5) and n = 6 (S24, P3XX). Top 100 DEGs per condition are reported in Supplementary Table 3.

a, Availability of TRs across GB states. Left: Schematic illustrating how a TR can be selectively expressed in its native Topic but epigenetically primed in cells of alternative states. Right: Mean chromatin accessibility (colour intensity) and mean expression (dot size) of indicated TRs across GB Topics. Bars on top indicate availability of TRs in Topics of alternative states, either by expression (scaled expression>0.5; purple) or epigenetic priming (scaled accessibility>0.5, scaled expression<0.3; green). b, Average expression (left) and chromatin accessibility (right) of the top TRs (activity score>0.05) of each target Topic within cells of each source Topic. TR expression is largely confined to Topics of the same GB state, whereas TR accessibility extends broadly to Topics of alternative states, indicating epigenetic priming for future activation. c, TAP between Topic pairs, scaled by the number of expressed TFs in the source Topic and by the weight of self-regulatory links in the target Topic. Asterisks denote significant links, defined as those exceeding the 95th percentile of a null distribution from 1,000 randomized GRNs (one-sided permutation test). OPC-NPC-like (25, 34) and AC-like (9, 44) tTopics show multiple strong links towards alternative state Topics, whereas links from neuronal-like Topics remain largely within their own state. Full list of TAP scores provided in Supplementary Table 4. d, Changes in TAP scores when using TR accessibility or expression in source Topic for computation. Positive values indicate TAP links mainly influenced by epigenetic priming of TRs, which encompass many of the links between different states. e, Number of top TRs from alternative states (activity score>0.5) that are epigenetically primed in each GB state. The epigenetic priming of alternative state TRs reflects transition potential patterns. f, Variance component analysis of TAP scores across Topic pairs. Each bar shows the proportion of variance explained by a single biological feature, fitted separately in an ordinary least squares model and stratified by whether the target Topic belongs to the same/related state (yellow; n = 77 Topic pairs), an alternative state (orange; n = 212), or any state (purple; n = 289). Regulatory links inferred from the eGRNs explain the largest share of TAP variance. For transitions towards alternative states, epigenetic priming of TRs contributes more than their expression level. g, TRS values between pairs of Topics. Neuronal-like Topics (24, 37) exert the highest repressive effects towards alternative state Topics. Asterisks label significant TRS links, estimated as in c. Full list of TRS values provided in Supplementary Table 4. h, Repression exerted by each source Topic towards the top 50 marker genes from each state identified by the linear model in Fig. 1b, instead of TRs. Similar to TR-level repression, neuronal-like Topics (24, 49) exert the strongest repression towards genes of alternative states. i, Cumulative repression exerted by individual source Topics towards genes of alternative Topics or states. Neuronal-like Topic 24 exerts the strongest repression against alternative identities. j,k, Net transition potential between Topics, as determined by the difference between TAP and TRS values between Topic pairs. Three distinct regulatory mechanisms underlie net transition potential interactions with alternative Topics: (i) predominant repression (Topic 24), (ii) predominant activation (Topics 9 and 34), and (iii) limited activation or repression (Topic 19). Raw values are provided in Supplementary Table 4. Illustration in a created in BioRender; Mall, M. https://biorender.com/51tfsoq (2026).

a, Schematic of dorsal telencephalon development, depicting neurogenic and gliogenic differentiation trajectories from radial glia towards differentiated neuronal and glial cell types. The shown differentiation hierarchy was reconstructed from available lineage-tracing studies49,50,51. NPC: Neural progenitor cell, OPC: Oligodendrocyte precursor cell, GPC: Glial progenitor cell. b, Activity of selected Topics inferred by scDORI from a developmental brain atlas (n = 12 donors)48. Colour denotes average Topic activity scaled across cell types of dorsal telencephalic origin, collected during early fetal, late fetal, and post-natal development stages. Topic-regulated programs are labelled on the right, determined based on Topic activity patterns, associated genes, and TF regulators. UL: Upper-layer, DL: Deep-layer. Full list of inferred Topics reported in Supplementary Table 5. c, TRs identified in developmental Topics in b recovered canonical lineage regulators, including PAX6 and GLI3 in radial glia114, SOX11 in fetal neurons115, CUX2 in UL neurons116, FOXP2 in DL neurons117, SOX9 in astrocytes118, OLIG1 in OPCs119, and MYRF in oligodendrocytes120, indicating high-confidence prediction of bona fide fate regulators. d, TAP, TRS and net transition potential (TAP–TRS) between pairs of developmental Topics in b. Shown are the respective values scaled by the number of TFs in the source Topic and self-activation in the target Topic. Asterisks denote significant links, defined as those exceeding the 95th percentile of a null distribution from 1,000 randomized GRNs (one-sided permutation test). Progenitor Topics show broad transition potential toward downstream lineages, whereas terminally differentiated cell type Topics show little or no transition potential towards alternative lineages, often constrained by repression. These results reflect the canonical differentiation hierarchy shown in a, as well as dedifferentiation potentials described for OPCs and astrocytes51,52, demonstrating that our transition model captures biologically coherent relationships. Illustration in a created in BioRender; Mall, M. https://biorender.com/51tfsoq (2026).

a, Schematic of the approach used to compute spatial co-activity of Topics across 97 matched tumour sections profiled by Visium spatial transcriptomics. For every section and Topic pair, the pairwise Euclidean distance between Topic A and Topic B spots is computed. Spatial co-activity is defined as the fraction of sections in which the closest 10% of spot pairs are spatially overlapping. Because spatial distance is symmetric by construction, net transition potentials (TAP–TRS) are symmetrized before row-wise Pearson correlation. b, Number of Visium sections and patients represented per Topic pair in the analysis described in a. All Topic pairs were covered by at least 20 sections derived from at least 7 patients, supporting the generalizability of the reported spatial co-activity patterns. Data are presented as mean ± s.d. c, Average spatial co-activity between Topic pairs computed as described in a (right), compared to their symmetric net transition potentials (left). Topic pairs with high net transition potential tend to be spatially co-active, as evidenced by row-wise correlations (Pearson r, right bar). Asterisks denote correlation P < 0.05. A full list of spatial co-activity values between Topics is provided in Supplementary Table 6. d, Schematic of how temporal co-activity of Topics was computed across pseudotime-aligned clonal trajectories. For each Topic pair, we averaged the cosine similarity of their temporal profiles across the top 10% of trajectories in which the two Topics were most temporally proximal, and compared the resulting matrix to net transition potential using column-wise (r1) and row-wise (r2) Pearson correlations, which capture incoming and outgoing transition relationships, respectively. e, Number of clonal populations per patient considered for the temporal analysis in d. A total of 57 clonal trajectories from all 12 patients were considered. f, Average temporal co-activity of Topics as described in d,e compared to net transition potentials (left). Topic pairs with high net transition potential tended to be temporally co-active for incoming and outgoing transitions, as evidenced by column-wise (top bar) and row-wise (right bar) correlations. Asterisks denote correlation P < 0.05. A full list of temporal co-activity values between Topics is provided in Supplementary Table 7. g, Correlation between Topic spatial co-activity and symmetric net transition potentials associated with each source Topic (n = 17). TAP and TRS values were computed using Topic-specific scDORI eGRNs, a union scDORI eGRN pooling links across Topics, SCENIC+ eGRNs, or random eGRNs. Dot colour represents the source Topic. Topic-specific scDORI eGRNs result in significantly higher correlation with spatial co-activity patterns than those derived using alternative GRNs (P = 0.0057 vs. Union; P = 0.0117 vs SCENIC+; paired two-sided t-test). h, Same as in g, but correlating temporal co-activity patterns in f and net transition potentials. Values denote the average between column-wise (incoming links, r1) and row-wise (outgoing links, r2) correlations for each Topic. Net transition potential values estimated with Topic-specific scDORI eGRNs positively correlated with temporal co-activity, significantly outperforming those derived from alternative methods (P = 0.0052 vs. Union; P = 0.0026 vs SCENIC+; paired two-sided t-test). i, Average epigenetic plasticity of cells in each Topic (as in Fig. 1c, top 5,000 cells per Topic) compared with (i) the cumulative net transition potential towards alternative state Topics (Topic-driven plasticity) and (ii) the total repression exerted by each Topic, both computed from Topic-specific scDORI eGRNs, a union scDORI eGRN pooling links across Topics, or SCENIC+ eGRNs. Topic-specific scDORI eGRNs best recapitulate observed epigenetic plasticity, with modelled plasticity and repression showing significant positive (r = 0.71, P = 0.002) and negative (r = −0.512, P = 0.036) correlations, respectively. Yellow boxes indicate P < 0.05. Box plots in g,h show median and IQR; whiskers are 1.5 × IQR. Illustrations in a,d created in BioRender; Mall, M. https://biorender.com/51tfsoq (2026).

a, Predicted regulatory roles of indicated neuronal-like TFs based on scDORI. Heat map colours indicate differences in the number of activated and repressed marker genes of each Topic (top 250). Dot size and colour denote TF-driven regulation of target TRs (TAP/TRS analysis, Supplementary Table 4). Manchester United and Tottenham are continuing to keep a close eye on Morgan Gibbs-White as speculation builds around the Nottingham Forest captain’s long-term future.

The England international remains one of Forest’s most influential players and is still central to Oliver Glasner’s plans, but his performances have ensured interest from bigger clubs has not disappeared.

With both United and Spurs looking at ways to add more creativity and goals from midfield, Gibbs-White is an obvious player to monitor.

According to TEAMtalk, Forest have no desire to sell Gibbs-White and continue to view him as a major part of their project.

Tottenham’s interest is well established after they came close to signing him in 2025, while Manchester United have also tracked the midfielder as they assess longer-term options in the No.10 role.

Forest strengthened their position by tying Gibbs-White down to a new contract, and previous TEAMtalk reporting has suggested it would take an exceptional offer to convince the club to reconsider.

The midfielder produced 25 goal contributions in 53 appearances last season, further increasing his value.

A recent CaughtOffside report also states that Tottenham remain interested and could revisit the deal if Gibbs-White becomes available. The report adds that Forest’s difficult start to the season may eventually influence his thinking.

From Forest’s perspective, selling Gibbs-White in January would make little sense.

They are fighting to move away from the wrong end of the Premier League table, and losing their captain midway through the season could seriously weaken Glasner’s side. Football Insider has also reported that Forest are confident he will remain at the City Ground in January despite continued interest.

The more interesting question is what happens next summer.

Gibbs-White is now 26 and entering the stage of his career where Champions League football could become a major priority.

Man United could see him as a future successor to Bruno Fernandes, while Tottenham already know exactly what he can bring.

Forest still hold the power for now, but if Gibbs-White decides the time has come for a bigger stage, interest from United and Spurs is unlikely to be the only competition.

#1388. Sarri: ‘Atalanta conceded a stupid goal, but with 14 players out, we take the point’

Maurizio Sarri insists Atalanta ‘will take the point’ against Kairat Almaty, despite ‘conceding a stupid goal,’ and hope to secure Conference League qualification ‘when we have more of our squad available.’

La Dea badly needed a victory to boost morale as well as their standing in the Conference League after a win over Pafos and 2-0 defeat away to Ajax, but it was only a meagre point at home against Kazakh side Kairat Almaty.

They had gone behind to a classic counter-attack from Marc Gual, but managed to claw back an equaliser with substitute Nikola Krstovic.

“If you have 14 players out at the same time, and you consider this a week to relaunch the season, that seems tough,” Sarri told Sky Sport Italia.

“We had 10 players injured today, plus four who the medical staff told us should not be used for more than 30 minutes. We certainly could’ve won tonight if we hadn’t conceded a stupid goal, then it became an uphill struggle.

“Fortunately we didn’t give up, so we tried to the end to bring home a positive result. It was a struggle, we moved the ball around too slowly and failed to find spaces in a very defensive opponent.

“With so many difficulties that we were dealing with, we take the point and hope to secure qualification later in the tournament, when we have more of our squad available.”

Atalanta have not won any of their last seven matches between Serie A and the Conference League, and went into a three-day training retreat after Monday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Parma.

Considering the side that Sarri put out this evening, did he expect better from his players?

“One always expects a lot from his players. Gianluca Scamacca was injured, so I only saw him train for the first time yesterday, so it’s hard to expect much more from him right now.

“Undoubtedly, I expected more from a few players, but we are in a period where we’re playing eight games in 23 days and forced to do it with the same limited group.”

It was always going to be difficult for Sarri to get Atalanta to adapt to his very different style of football after more than a decade in the Gian Piero Gasperini vein, but the injury crisis has slowed that process further.

“Clearly, this is a big transformation, and then if we have added difficulties like this… Tonight we played two defenders from the Under-23 team who only really have experience in Serie C, plus Kamaldeen Sulemana who got hurt on August 2 and has only been back with the team for four or five days.

“It’s also tough because none of the players have history with me, so what was already a complex process has had new layers of difficulty put on top.”

Having a bunch of youth players in the side gets them blooded and looks like there are real talents in there (Obric and Idele look quality but need experience). Not only that, in the last few games they have been hit on the counter after dominating the first halves. Though a comeback to a point is a positive.

#1387. Matheus Cunha's lucky escape: Man United star to AVOID further UEFA punishment after returning to Old Trafford pitch despite red card in Roma comeback win - with Michael Carrick escorting him off again

Published: 10:00 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 10:18 EDT, 4 November 2026

Matheus Cunha has avoided any further punishment after coming back onto the pitch at the end of Manchester United’s momentous Champions League win over Roma despite having been sent off.

United’s matchwinner reacted angrily to being told by head coach Michael Carrick and backroom staff not to celebrate with his teammates on the grass because he risked breaking UEFA rules and incurring more than an automatic one-match ban.

But a UEFA spokesman confirmed on Wednesday that Cunha is not facing any additional action, and will only miss the next Champions League game against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal later this month.

He said: ‘The UEFA official reports did not mention anything about this incident. Therefore the automatic one-match ban following two yellow cards should not be extended for this reason. We are not investigating further this matter.’

Cunha starred in the 3-2 comeback victory at Old Trafford, winning a penalty that Bruno Fernandes converted for the first goal and then scoring the other two himself.

However, the Brazil star was sent off in injury-time for picking up two yellow cards in quick succession, the first for taking his shirt off after scoring the winner and the second for a needless foul on Leonardo Balerdi.

Carrick stepped in to order Cunha down the tunnel to keep the sent-off star out of further trouble and avoid a repeat of his costly protest at Wolves last year https://t.co/Gd379NbHd3 via @MailSport #mufc

Matheus Cunha completed a memorable Man United comeback with a fierce strike

He was booked for jumping into the Stretford End - and received a second yellow shortly after

Instead of going down the tunnel to the dressing-room, Cunha perched on an advertising board in the Stretford End to watch the remaining few minutes of the game and then came back onto the pitch after the final whistle.

United staff spotted the potential issue and Carrick ordered him back to the dressing-room to avoid further trouble. A visibly upset Cunha was then escorted towards the tunnel.

‘I was disappointed with how it finished, but again just shows how much he cares and is willing to do,’ said Carrick. ‘When he's in that frame of mind, he's in that mood and he plays like that, that's what we want from him. Matheus can do those things, you know.

‘He's got those moments. We put him inside and swapped him with Bryan (Mbeumo) at half-time to try and get him in the middle of the pitch, try and give us a little bit of different shape, and put him in the centre of the pitch, and he found himself in good positions.’

Cunha’s exit at Old Trafford was reminiscent of an incident in March 2025 when he was playing for Wolves.

He was charged by the FA for acting in an improper manner after he was sent off in the FA Cup defeat to Bournemouth after clashing with Milos Kerkez in the final minute of extra-time and then had to be escorted down the tunnel. Cunha was later handed an additional one-match ban and fined £50,000 for his behaviour.

Arsenal and Manchester City are continuing to monitor Newcastle United defender Tino Livramento as uncertainty begins to grow over his long-term future at St James’ Park.

The 23-year-old has been admired by both clubs for some time, with his ability to operate on either side of defence making him particularly attractive to teams demanding tactical flexibility from their full-backs.

Newcastle remain determined to keep him, but his contract situation could eventually force them into a difficult decision.

According to Football Insider, Arsenal and City are tracking Livramento closely after previously seeing approaches for the England international blocked by Newcastle.

His current contract runs until 2028, but Newcastle would reportedly consider a sale next summer if they cannot make meaningful progress over an extension before then. The Magpies would prefer to agree fresh terms and still regard Livramento as an important long-term player.

Livramento’s quality has never really been in doubt.

Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe praised him during an injury update earlier this year, saying: “He’s an outstanding player.” Howe also highlighted how impressive the defender had been when consistently available.

It is easy to understand why Arsenal and City remain interested.

Livramento is quick, technically comfortable and capable of playing at both right-back and left-back. That versatility would suit Mikel Arteta particularly well, while City could view him as a long-term option for the right side of their defence.

A fresh CaughtOffside report also confirms that both clubs are monitoring the situation, with Newcastle reluctant to sell unless contract negotiations fail.

The obvious concern is Livramento’s injury record. He started only 14 Premier League matches last season and has managed just 33 league minutes so far this campaign. Newcastle are currently taking a cautious approach to his latest recovery.

That makes any huge transfer fee difficult to justify right now.

However, if Livramento can stay fit and Newcastle fail to secure a new contract, next summer could become an interesting opportunity. Arsenal and City clearly see the talent, the question is whether his body can allow him to fulfil it consistently.

Man United, Arsenal and Chelsea scout £50m-rated midfielder during UCL display

Bayern Munich are reportedly not currently expected to be in the mix for Paris Saint-Germain winger Desire Doue, who is also being linked with Chelsea.

Doue has been a star player for PSG and it surely wouldn’t make sense for them to sell the talented 21-year-old at this stage, when he looks like he’s only going to continue getting better and better.

Chelsea were recently linked with Doue by TEAMtalk, but Christian Falk has played down the prospect of Bayern being in the race for his signature in today’s CF Bayern Insider column.

This could perhaps be a boost for the Blues, but in truth, it doesn’t necessarily seem like it will ultimately make much difference, with TEAMtalk also having reported on Doue looking likely to sign a new contract at the Parc des Princes.

Doue would surely be a fine signing for Bayern, but Falk has played down the links, saying: “It is NOT TRUE: Bayern Munich have joined Premier League clubs in holding interest in Désiré Doué.

“He’s a very exciting player, and Bayern tried to get him at Säbener Straße but it was too expensive at the time and he decided to go to Paris. It’s one of those transfers where you feel, if you couldn’t sign him as a young talent when everyone wanted him, you’re not going to sign him as a more seasoned professional.

“He’s doing so well in Paris, and there’s just no chance of Bayern paying the price PSG would want (though they don’t want to sell him) for the attacker’s services.

“I’m very sorry, but it’s just too late to make this transfer for Bayern Munich. The silver lining, of course, is that Bayern caught on very early how good this player could be, so it’s clear that Bayern Munich’s instincts are very much on the money.

“However, they don’t have the money, like other clubs do, to stockpile players in this age range.”

PSG did well to snap up Doue when they did, and he’s gone on to become a star player for them, so any prospect of a transfer to other major clubs seems very slim right now, and will likely remain so for the foreseeable future.

#1384. Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change

Sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

On TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN

Fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their new head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

United’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M

But, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

Might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh

I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

We wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a big team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so important for us.

There were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

In the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

It was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

The defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

Manchester United play Spurs when the Premier League returns in three weeks, in a game that will feel huge.

5 - With five points, this is Manchester United's joint-lowest tally after five games of a Premier League season, also picking up five in 2014-15.Sluggish. pic.twitter.com/UZTBWRpGnm

Fulham remain winless but the draw lifts them above Spurs, who will spend the international break at the foot of the table. On this evidence, both of these teams are in for a struggle relative to expectations.

Fulham wanted a free-kick on the edge of the box for a sliding challenge on Kevin for Maguire but the referee decides he got the ball.

United break forward and win a corner. It comes for Martinez who shifts his feet to shoot with his right foot and the goal-bound effort was blocked!

Just the three minutes of added time to play, but United are the team pushing forward searching for an unlikely winner.

United may have just spared themselves a damaging defeat, and there might just be time to go on an win this. Cunha with a speculative shot from outside the box, and Affengruber extends his left leg to block the shot but the deflection leaves Leno stranded. A stroke of luck for United but Fulham have invited it.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M

Bassey now penalised for a high boot on Dalot, United free-kick on the halfway line. Fulham just about standing firm, and they are helped when a crossfield pass towards Dorgu bounces off for a throw-in.

United with another corner and there are loud appeals for a handball penalty against Bassey, the proximity was very close but his hand was up. But VAR takes a look and the fact the hand was tucked in towards his chest spares the Fulham defender.

Fulham and the home crowd happy with a goal kick after an overhit cross towards Shaw at the back post. Dorgu has been sent on in Carrick’s last throw of the dice, replacing Shaw at left-back.

You would not say United are pulling Fulham from pillar to post, it feels a little hopeful, but it is one-way traffic. An attack against defence session in Fulham’s half. Charles and Kevin do well to relieve the pressure momentarily, but United are back on the attack again.

Here are those changes: Mason Mount on for Kobbie Mainoo for United, while Andersen replaces King for the home team. Arbeloa happy to hold what he has. Lisandro Martinez volleys a shot over the bar.

Positive first involvement from Zirkzee, releasing Mbeumo, but the Fulham defenders read his intentions and blocked the shot after he cut inside. Joachim Andersen is preparing to come on for Fulham, as is Mason Mount for United.

Much better from Fulham, another attack started by Bassey reading play just like the goal, but this time Lammens’s wrists were strong to parry Kevin’s shot. Rashford is then flagged offside.

Fulham change: Larsson is on for Berge, Sweden for Norway. And Carrick has brought on Zirkzee for Rashford. Famous last words, but does that make you more likely to score a goal? Not that Rashford can feel hard done to.

The United forward was falling over, but he generated enough power to trouble the goalkeeper. From the corner, Maguire picks up the ball on the far side and chips a cross over the blue shirts in the middle.

Kevin sold himself in a one-on-one with Rashford, but King did well to put his foot in at the edge of the box and the ball bounces through kindly to Leno. Tielemans then misplaces a pass when United were in a promising position.

If United had played like this from the start of the second half they would not be losing, but now they have just 20 minutes plus stoppage time to overturn the deficit.

Fulham making a double sub: Kevin and Palacios on for Iwobi and Bobb.

United have roused themselves since conceding, winning a flurry of corners.

What a save from Leno! Mbeumo’s curling shot from outside the box was arcing beautifully into the far corner, but the German goalkeeper tipped his effort around the post.

Then Maguire is eased out at the back post, and Fulham breathe a sigh of relief.

Strong words from Gary Neville after the goal went it: “I’ve watched United since the age of five and that is the worst 15 minutes [from half-time to the goal] I have seen them play.”

Well doesn’t that just sum up United’s season so far. There are appeals for a foul on Cunha from Bassey, but the Fulham defender was stronger and he took some initiative to drive towards the box. Bassey let fly and kept his shot down, Lammens could only stick out a leg and the ball rebounded off the helpless Martinez and back into the net.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN

Fulham have a corner after it opened up nicely for Iwobi at the edge of the box, but his left-footed strike deflects behind. A very smooth footballer, but finishing has never been Iwobi’s strong suit. Fulham fail to make anything of the corner.

Fulham and United’s fans now urging their teams on after the game halted to glacial pace. Nothing much happening at all since the start of the second half.

Gary Neville growing increasingly frustrated by the lack of intensity out of possession by both teams: “Never walk on a football pitch.” Questions have been asked of United’s fitness levels and physical readiness for the new season. Fulham enjoying a spell of possession in United’s half again.

More from Neville: “It’s like it’s time for the whites to play against the blue mannequins, before they reverse it up the other end. One thing I do know, I’ve played in a lot of football matches, it’s not right.”

There has been a real lack of conviction in Rashford’s play in the final third, this time it was underhit pass across the box towards Mbeumo which was cut out. Good ball by Tielemans to release Rashford, but no end product again.

Sir Alex Ferguson is watching on at Craven Cottage. The game has slipped into one of its lulls again.

Nice football from Fulham involving Charles and Iwobi but United break forward after a loose touch by Bobb. Fernandes did well to keep the ball and wait for support, and Castagne is booked for a block on Rashford.

The first few minutes of the half are played deep in Fulham’s territory, but United’s delivery from wide is not good enough and Cunha is penalised for a foul in the middle in any case.

At half-time that is another worrying performance from Manchester United. Yes, they could be ahead and have created chances, with Bruno Fernandes hitting the post. But on the balance of play they should be behind with Fulham’s 19-year-old Josh King the best player on the pitch and United reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Michael Carrick has more work to do during the interval than Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and cannot be happy with how defensively vulnerable his team and but also how wasteful they are in front of goal.

Both teams will believe they should have scored in that first half in a game that has oscillated between periods of passivity and flurries of goal-mouth action. When United speed up their interplay, it looks like they can cut through Fulham, but Carrick’s team’s box defending leaves much to be desired. There were 26 shots on goal without reward in that 45 minutes.

Another chance is missed, this time Rashford with a side foot over the bar from a Cunha cross that took a nick on the way through. Always leaning back, poor technique from a player of his standing.

Fulham then throw a punch back, but King is booked for diving after pushing the ball beyond Maguire. The attacker is not happy, but not sure he can have any complaints.

United almost caught out by a one-two between Iwobi and Garcia, but Lammens rushes off his line to get there first. Both attacks look to have the beating of both defences, but somehow there have been no goals.

United’s best move of the game, starting with a whipped pass from Tielemans when under pressure into Dalot who turns into space inside. Fernandes could have taken a shot on himself from the edge of the box, but he moved the ball on to Rashford but his side-foot shot was tame and straight at Leno.

The game has settled after that flurry of chances when both teams could easily have scored. Fulham do well to block Rashford’s sight of goal as he cuts inside looking for a shot, and then Mbeumo commits a foul.

Cunha with a deflected strike from distance, which arcs over Leno and glances off the post! The sort of deflection that gives a goalkeeper no chance, Leno was scrambling.

Mainoo’s shot is blocked from the corner, and then Fulham break forward with numbers. Iwobi picks out Josh King in the box, and Lammens sticks out a right leg to keep out his driven shot.

Josh King is again showing why he was so close to a full England call-up. The 19-year-old is at the heart of the action as Fulham continue to create chance after chance against a very shaky Manchester United defence who have been reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

This stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

Fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

Bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

Josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

Fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

The interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

Fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

Bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

United have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

Fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

Promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

If Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

Michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

JJ Gabriel has been in the news this week, and Sam Wallace writes in his column this week that the battle to sign up and coming academy players is growing ever more fierce between Premier League clubs. Managers are handing out debuts earlier and earlier to satisfy the demands of the best young players, and an increasing number of clubs are happy to gamble significant fees and wages on potental.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia

Subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe

Here's how The Fulham shape up. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/0IxS0J3ldf

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊

The script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a big impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager said.

“That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

“But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he said it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

The mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and new head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

#1383. Newcastle Confidential: REVEALED - Players 'confused' by Matthias Jaissle's instructions, why formation tweak is a possibility, Joelinton injury worry and new transfer guru's methods explained

Published: 12:00 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 12:01 EDT, 4 November 2026

Newcastle’s players are ‘confused’ by what Matthias Jaissle wants from them, a source close to the dressing room has told me.

I've been told the squad remains supportive of Jaissle and there is a determination to get things right for the head coach – senior players accept there is a responsibility on them – but there is also a desire for clarity over what it is they are being asked to do on the field.

Jaissle said in the wake of Monday's 1-0 home defeat by Everton that he could not understand why the team had not followed his instructions and executed the tactics they had worked on in training. He said the plan was not to play ‘long balls’.

Sources also say Jaissle spoke to his players afterwards about their press not being what he wanted and their passing being too slow in the opposition half.

However, I have been told some players are unsure as to the playing style and strategy, and that has led to those in deep positions getting the ball forward as quickly as possible, invariably with a long pass. There are also some within the dressing room wondering why the team continues to play with a No 10 when they do not have a specialist in that position.

Another source close to a senior player says the logical solution is a return to the 4-3-3 of recent seasons. There was word from inside the training ground that Jaissle was considering such a change ahead of the trip to Crystal Palace last month, so it is not off the table.

The demand from supporters to find a place for teenager Sean Steur in the midfield could yet see a tweak to the system, especially as Jaissle believes he and Nico Gonzalez are not suited to playing together as a two.

Newcastle's players are understood to be 'confused' by what it is head coach Matthias Jaissle wants from them

The demand from supporters to find a place for teenager Sean Steur (left) in the midfield could yet see a tweak to the Newcastle system

Joelinton is a fresh injury concern and medical staff will know in the next 24 hours if he is set to miss Saturday’s trip to Fulham, I can reveal. The Brazilian was feeling some muscle discomfort post-match on Monday and there is hope that the issue is related to a severe case of cramp.

However, I understand that is yet to be confirmed and, given Joelinton’s history of muscle strains, including his hamstring, no chances will be taken. The 30-year-old only returned from a thigh injury three weeks ago having been sidelined since the summer.

In better news, Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Lewis Miley are set to return for the game at Craven Cottage.

I understand Fernandez-Pardo wanted to be included in the squad for the visit of Everton but was told by staff he needed more training. The Belgian had missed the previous two matches with what is being described as a ‘tricky virus’ and only returned to training over the weekend.

Fernandez-Pardo arrived on Tyneside insisting he wanted to be used as a central striker following his £51million move from Lille. However, Jaissle currently prefers William Osula in that position and Fernandez-Pardo will likely be competing for a place out wide at Craven Cottage.

Miley, meanwhile, was also pushing for involvement on Monday after recovering from a glute issue. The 20-year-old’s return is timely given the midfield struggles of late, as well as the fresh worry over Joelinton and Jacob Ramsey’s suspension following his red card against Everton.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is available again for Newcastle after suffering with a ‘tricky virus’

One player who almost certainly won’t come in for a start is Aladji Bamba, although we are told he will NOT be going out on loan in January.

The 20-year-old has appeared for just 27 minutes since his £30m arrival from Monaco in the summer, and he has not featured at all since September 19.

But despite potential availability issues in midfield, Jaissle does not feel Bamba is ready to start Premier League matches. That has led to a suggestion among some that he could be loaned out in January, especially as he has made only 12 senior starts in his career.

However, I understand the plan is for Bamba to remain on Tyneside and there has been encouragement with his recent performances in training.

Aladji Bamba has impressed in training of late and won't leave on loan in January despite his lack of first-team minutes

It has been interesting speaking to those who know a little more about Newcastle's new head of recruitment Tomas Amaral, who was virtually unknown in the UK before his appointment last month.

The Portuguese, 35, has been described as a 'bookworm and laptop obsessive', a meticulous talent-spotter who works long into the night. Amaral, who spent four years scouting for Benfica and was most recently sporting director at Spartak Moscow, has also spoken previously of the dangers of clubs signing good players who do not fit the manager's system.

He believes recruitment should begin with a clear footballing identity, rather than collecting talented individuals and hoping they somehow fit together. He also argues that scouts should challenge managers over transfer targets, rather than simply indulge their wishes.

Interestingly, his recruitment strategy involves two lists – one identifying players good enough for the club, the other those specifically suited to the manager's demands. For him, character and adaptability are considered just as important as ability.

He was part of the Benfica scouting team who identified Enzo Fernandez when signing him from River Plate in 2022. The midfielder was sold to Chelsea for a near £100m profit the following year.

Amaral’s arrival at least gives clarity to the recruitment structure inside St James’ Park, and he would appear to have a busy 12 months ahead given what feel like obvious areas for improvement across the pitch. I understand there is scope to spend in January should the club feel it necessary.

Beneath first-team level, Newcastle have cast their scouting net a little wider this week with two promising teenagers from Gambia arriving on Tyneside.

We understand Omar Marong and Alieu Saine, both 16, will stay for a two-week trial and train with the academy. They are products of the Today Makes Tomorrow Academy and have been identified under the club’s new global talent drive.

The pair caught the eye during Gambia’s triumph at September’s West African Under-17 Championship. Central midfielder Marong captained the side, while winger Saine finished as joint-top scorer with four goals. Neither player can join permanently until turning 18 because of FIFA regulations, but Newcastle are keen to assess their potential.

Meanwhile, the club are also set to appoint a specialist scout in Africa.

Finally, Newcastle prospect Matheos Ferreira could soon be at the centre of an international tug of war.

The 18-year-old, born in Ashington and raised in Berwick, has been called up by Brazil Under 20s for friendlies against Japan and Singapore this month. He is the only English-based player in the squad.

Newcastle prospect Matheos Ferreira could play for England, Italy or Brazil

But Ferreira, whose father is Brazilian and mother Italian, also qualifies for England and Italy. He has previously represented England at youth level and recently obtained an Italian passport.

I have seen him play a handful of times and there is certainly plenty of talent and potential. Interestingly, he has been operating as a No 10 at times this season, having come through the ranks as a winger.

Maybe there is a No 10 inside the club after all…

#1382. UEL | AZ Alkmaar 1-2 Juventus: Special K success in Alkmaar

Juventus secured an impressive 2-1 win away to AZ Alkmaar, who were unbeaten at home in Europe for over three years, as Teun Koopmeiners and Randal Kolo Muani kept strong Europa League form going.

The Bianconeri had a much-needed 2-0 victory over Napoli on Sunday and were unbeaten in the Europa League with two wins and a 2-2 draw against Rennes. Injuries continued to pile up, as Weston McKennie joined Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Nico Gonzalez, Francisco Conceicao, Zeki Celik, Khephren Thuram and Kamil Grabara on the treatment table, so Jeff Ekhator was added to the UEFA list.

Teun Koopmeiners faced his younger brother Peer, with both coming up through the AZ youth academy, and the crowd had a pre-match banner depicting them as children. The Dutch side lost the opening Europa League fixture at Sunderland, then beat Hapoel Beer Sheva and Ararat-Armenia, but were unbeaten in 17 UEFA home fixtures stretching back to October 2023.

Jeroen Zoet, Jizz Hornkamp, Wouter Goes and Stije Resink were out of action, but Kees Smit was back in the squad for the first time since September 20. They lost their last two Eredivisie games without finding the net.

Randal Kolo Muani’s angled drive flashed across the face of goal to skim the far post, and the ex-PSG man was instrumental in the opening goal.

Kolo Muani flicked the ball up over a defender to get down the right and pulled back to the edge of the area, where Teun Koopmeiners was ready to sweep in with the inside of the left boot. The midfielder did not celebrate against his hometown club, with his brother captaining them.

Things went from bad to worse for the hosts, who were forced into a change for the Lewis Schouten injury moments later.

Kerim Alajbegovic’s scorcher skimmed the crossbar at the far top corner from just inside the box, but AZ Alkmaar started to push back, Guglielmo Vicario right behind the deflected Dave Kwakman strike.

Juventus doubled their lead when a high Kolo Muani press forced Mees de Wit into an error, Nick Woltemade returning the pass for the Frenchman to bend the left-foot finish into the far bottom corner.

Alajbegovic hesitated when Teun Koopmeiners intercepted a mistaken Jari De Busser pass and the chance went begging, then Federico Gatti sprinted from his own half only to over-hit the final ball for Kolo Muani.

Smit came off the bench and saw his effort charged down by Lloyd Kelly, then fired another very promising attempt over from 12 yards while the hosts had penalty appeals rejected when Elijah Dijkstra went down under pressure from Kelly.

AZ Alkmaar did eventually get back into the game when Ayoub Oufkir robbed Kelly at the touchline and sent Dijkstra down the right, pulling back for Mexx Meerdink to tap in from close range.

Suddenly the hosts were fired up and had the ball in the net again during added time, but Meerdink was offside when his header forced an extraordinary Guglielmo Vicario save, so the rebound from Mees de Wit did not count.

The pressure was on to the final whistle, including a Smit free kick into the crowd that could’ve gone anywhere, but Juve held on.

T Koopmeiners 19 (J), Kolo Muani 37 (J), Meerdink 88 (A)
