#1351. Kane’s record-equalling cap was no different to his first

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he said. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”

One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

“Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

England kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

England lead! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿⚽️ A great ball from Kane and a great finish from Coufal - unfortunately for the defender, it's in the wrong net...🫣 https://t.co/h54xQnunZM

The second goal, on 40 minutes, was one for the ages. Anderson’s ball out to the right was met first time by Rogers for the cross and Kane ran into the space, as he has done so many times, to deliver a finish struck with customary assuredness. Bellingham almost flicked in Rogers’s cross on 56 minutes and from the corner that came after, Kane nodded in a header at the back post from Lewis Hall’s cross. All said, the defending was woeful but there was nothing wrong with the finish.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and said he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

“It means a lot,” Tuchel said. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel said: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

But on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

“We had these experiences together and we had a big tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

“We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”

We played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

[Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find new words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

[Has the World Cup made England stronger?]  Of course, we got the first medal in 60 years. We didn’t go out in the group stage. We had a strong qualification, strong World Cup and strong camp. All four matches were on a high level. The camp throughout from the first day was on the highest level. You learn every day together. We grew stronger.

I was happy that everyone who was in the camp was contributing. Everyone was on the pitch. Everyone showed he was willing to give everything for the team and for the shirt. The guys who were with us for the World Cup set the standards high, made everyone feel welcome and everyone had a good camp.

He’s the best England player evert to wear the shirt and it’s an honour to play with him. And he’s only getting better.

A perfect night for me personally and also for the team. It’s been a tough camp, a long camp with some difficult games so it’s nice to finish it off all together. An extremely proud evening for me.

You saw some fantastic football out there tonight. The way we’re moving, the one-touch stuff, a fantastic ball from Elliot to Morgan and then a first time cross which was as good as it gets. As a striker you’re just waiting for those opportunities.

It started in the first game [reaching a higher level] although the result didn’t go for us. First game after a tournament, obviously this was a four-game camp, we had to find it [a higher level] and find it quickly. That’s the most pleasing thing.

This is the England team. There’s always going to be competition for places. It’s about taking the opportunity whether it’s 90 minutes, five minutes, whatever it was, make the most of it. You’re seeing that, everyone wants to be part of this. That’s only going to make us better for sure.

[Now for cap 126 next month?] That would be nice for sure.

Because places between teams who finish on the same points in the first instance are decided on head-to-heads, Croatia will have to beat England 8-0 at Wembley next month to have any hope of stopping them from qualifying for the quarter-finals.

First win at Wembley in four, three wins in succession, 14 goals in four games and three clean sheets in a row.

Shilton’s took him 20 years as Gordon Banks was simply too good in the couple of years following his debut and then a couple of managers, Don Revie and Ron Greenwood, preferred Ray Clemence until the latter finally plumped for Shilton as No 1 in 1979. Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

England played the Czech Republic a week ago, winning 2-0 in Prague by virtue of Anthony Gordon’s cute header and Kane’s clever shot through a defender’s legs but they huffed and puffed for ages against a team harshly reduced to 10 men until they blew the house down. They went on to marmalise Croatia 7-0 in their next game in front of a crowd that sounded like a cross between the choirs on Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2 and There’s No One Quite Like Grandma.

In the past England have had problems backing up their best performances – the 4-1 evisceration of the Dutch at Euro 96 was followed by the cagey display in the quarter-final against Spain before prevailing on penalties, the 5-1 victory in Munich in 2001 led to a drab 2-0 win against Albania at St James’ Park the following Tuesday, in 2016 they went to Berlin and beat world champions Germany but were thumped by Netherlands, who had not even qualified for Euro 2016, a couple of days later. Even their thrilling, second-half showing against Croatia in their World Cup opener in June preceded the dreary 0-0 draw with Ghana.

Given the attacking fluency in Rijeka, Thomas Tuchel must be tempted not to to ring the changes and replace seven or eight players. #1350. Alan Shearer: Two Liverpool Stars Worse Than Robertson After Summer Exit

Alan Shearer has highlighted Liverpool's "problem" at left-back and stated that the departed Andy Robertson is "better" than their two current options in the position.

Having joined the Reds from Hull City in 2017, the Scotland captain exited Anfield after nine years in the summer to join Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham team on a free transfer.

The 32-year-old has featured regularly for the Lilywhites since making the move, starting seven of their nine Premier League games so far this season.

On the other hand, Liverpool have rotated between Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas in both the Premier League and Champions League.

Andoni Iraola's team were on the losing side in the Champions League on Wednesday evening following a 3-2 defeat away at Fenerbahce, with Tsimikas struggling up against Mason Greenwood all game prior to Kerkez coming on his place.

Amid Liverpool's current struggles at left-back, Shearer gave his verdict on Iraola's current predicament and mentioned that the Reds let go of their best left-back during the summer.

"They've got a problem at left-back," said the Newcastle United legend when speaking on The Rest is Football podcast. "I mean, they let Robertson go when they've got Kerkez and Tsimikas.

I think Robertson is better than both of those two. I think there's problems, and it'll take a bit of time to sort it out.

Kerkez and Tsimikas' 2026/27 season in numbers

It is not the first time Kerkez has come in for criticism from Shearer after the former England international spoke about his concerns back in September 2025.

Struggling in his opening couple of months as a Liverpool player after faring so well for Bournemouth under Iraola, Shearer mentioned that the Reds were "not seeing the same player" in Kerkez after his outstanding performances down the left flank for the Cherries.

“Well, at the minute we’re not seeing the same player in Kerkez, particularly the left-hand side as we saw with Bournemouth," he said on NBC Sports.

“He was free-flowing. He had the license to go and roam and get forward. Here, to me it seems as if he’s caught in two minds whether he’s going to go, whether he’s going to stay and help protect that with Van Dijk and Konate.”

Kerkez has improved since his first few months at Liverpool but he's still not producing the levels he was on a regular basis during his time at Bournemouth.

Iraola is clearly the perfect man to get the best out of the Hungarian after doing so before, but he clearly has a huge challenge on his hands when it comes to Liverpool's issues at left-back.

If the Merseyside club continue to struggle there then the club may have no option but to upgrade in the position either in the January transfer window or next summer.

#1349. Forget Duran: Mika Baur is Celtic's Best Signing Since Arne Engels

Celtic finally kickstarted their Europa League campaign as they came from 1-0 down to beat Besiktas 3-2 at Parkhead on Thursday night.

Celtic came into the clash with the Turkish giants having lost all three of their Europa League fixtures this term, with two of those being at home to Ferencvaros and Celta Vigo.

It proved to be third time lucky for the Hoops at Parkhead as they saw off Besiktas, even though it looked like it could be the same old story for them in Europe when they went 1-0 down in the 54th minute.

The double introduction of Camilo Duran and Callum Osmand on the hour-mark changed the game in their favour, with the latter drawing the scoreline level just two minutes after coming on.

Duran then gave the hosts the lead in the 78th minute, before Orkun Kukcu equalised for the visitors in the 85th minute.

At that stage, fans may have thought that a draw was the most likely result, but Duran sent Celtic Park into raptures when he struck again in the 87th minute as they secured their first points of the campaign.

The Bhoys signed Duran for around £6m in the summer from Azerbaijani side Qarabag, but bigger things were expected from fellow attacking signing Kasper Hogh following his goalscoring exploits with Bodo/Glimt.

However, it has been the Colombia international who has been the star of the show in attack for O'Neill's men, taking his tally to 13 goals for the season on Thursday.

Meanwhile, Hogh has netted three times in 17 appearances for the Glasgow giants, although they all came in the same game against Kilmarnock back in August.

Duran is already a fan favourite unsurprisingly, but he isn't the only summer arrival shining in a green and white shirt.

Duran looks as though he can go on to become a future Celtic superstar based on what we've seen so far, but it is Mika Baur who is actually looking like the signing of the summer for the Hoops.

It has become painfully clear that the Glasgow outfit lack legs in midfield with captain Callum McGregor getting no younger, and O'Neill may have found the answer to the issue with Baur.

Celtic paid nearly £7m to sign the midfielder from Paderborn in the summer, but he is quickly establishing himself as one of the team's most important players.

Baur has been impressive whenever he has been on the pitch this term, but he hit new heights against Besiktas on Thursday, picking up Fotmob's second-highest rating for his performance, behind Duran.

The 22-year-old was absolutely everywhere as he helped Celtic secure their first Europa League points, proving he has the engine to be popping up all over the pitch.

It isn't just his off-the-ball work that is impressive though, as he is strong in possession too, as he showed against the Turkish club.

With some of Celtic's summer buys like Haissem Hassan, Hogh and Oliver Sorensen struggling to hit the ground running, it is refreshing to see how well Baur has started his Hoops career.

Sometimes there are players you can just tell are a step above at Celtic, with Arne Engels the last of those prior to his switch to West Ham United in the summer.

The early signs are that Baur is destined for big things, and he is quickly becoming the club's best signing since the Belgian star.

Celtic secured a 3-2 victory over Besiktas in the Europa League.

#1348. The Ins and Outs of Mancini’s latest Italy squad: 11 dropped, 8 new additions

Roberto Mancini named an Italy national team squad of 31 players on Thursday evening ahead of November’s Nations League fixtures against France and Belgium, but who dropped out and who are the new additions to the latest Azzurri squad?

Italy will be in action against France in San Siro next Thursday, November 12, and away against Belgium on Sunday, November 15.

As things stand, Italy sit in second place in their Nations League group on seven points after four matches. France lead the way on 10, Belgium are in third on six and Turkiye are bottom on zero.

After naming a squad of 34 players for his first camp back in charge of the Italy national team last month, Mancini has named a roster of 31 players this time around. 11 players that were named in Mancini’s squad back in September have dropped out and eight new faces have been called in.

Some of the players that have dropped out of the squad have returned to the U21s, where they will be more likely to gain playing time this break, including goalkeeper Massimo Pessina, defender Eddy Kouadio and striker Samuele Inacio.

Injuries have ruled Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Giacomo Raspadori and Moise Kean out of selection this time around.

The other names to drop out of the squad are Bryan Cristante, Rolando Mandragora, Daniel Maldini and Mohamed Ali Zoma.

As for the new additions, there is a return to the squad for Marco Palestra, who has recently made his first Premier League appearances with Chelsea after picking up an injury a few days before the season kicked off.

Niccolo Pisilli has returned, as has Samuele Ricci. The Como midfielder was not originally named in Mancini’s 34-man squad when it was announced in September, but was later called in as a replacement for Cristante, who left the camp through injury.

Completing the new additions are Alphadjo Cisse, Mattia Liberali, Luca Koleosho, Riccardo Cassano and Simone Lontani.

17-year-old Cassano and 18-year-old Lontani will be with the senior squad for a few days to train and effectively audition in front of Mancini, but will then return to the U18 and U19 squads later on in the week, where they will be more likely to earn minutes this break.

Out: Massimo Pessina (Bologna), Diego Coppola (Brighton), Giovanni Di Lorenzo (Napoli), Eddy Kouadio (Monza), Bryan Cristante (Roma), Rolando Mandragora (Torino), Samuele Inacio (Borussia Dortmund), Moise Kean (Como), Daniel Maldini (Cagliari), Giacomo Raspadori (Atalanta), Mohamed Ali Zoma (Nurnberg).

In: Marco Palestra (Chelsea), Riccardo Cassano (Como), Niccolo Pisilli (Roma), Samuele Ricci (Como), Simone Lontani (Parma), Alphadjo Cisse (Milan), Luca Koleosho (Paris FC), Mattia Liberali (Como).

Goalkeepers: Marco Carnesecchi (Atalanta), Gianluigi Donnarumma (Man City), Guglielmo Vicario (Juventus).

Defenders: Honest Ahanor (Crystal Palace), Alessandro Bastoni (Inter), Riccardo Calafiori (Arsenal), Federico Dimarco (Inter), Daniele Ghilardi (Roma), Michael Kayode (Brentford), Gianluca Mancini (Roma), Marco Palestra (Chelesa), Giorgio Scalvini (Atalanta).

Midfielders: Nicolò Barella (Inter), Riccardo Cassano (Como), Issa Doumbia (Sporting CP), Nicolò Fagioli (Fiorentina), Davide Frattesi (Lazio), Simone Lontani (Parma), Niccolò Pisilli (Roma), Samuele Ricci (Como), Alessandro Romano (Cagliari), Sandro Tonali (Tottenham).

Attackers: Nicolò Cambiaghi (Bologna), Alphadjo Cisse (Milan), Francesco Pio Esposito (Inter), Sebastiano Esposito (Sassuolo), Luca Koleosho (Paris FC), Mattia Liberali (Como), Gianluca Scamacca (Atalanta), Antonio Vergara (Napoli), Nicolo Zaniolo (Udinese).

#1347. Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool: Sloppy Reds wilt in Turkey again as Dirk Kuyt masterminds famous Champions League win against his error-strewn old side

Published: 14:54 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:15 EDT, 5 November 2026

The mad metropolis of Istanbul was the setting for one of Liverpool’s greatest nights, when this storied old club won the 2005 Champions League final down the road at the Ataturk Stadium – but right now fans will be glad to see the back of Turkey for a while.

For the third time in just over 13 months, the English giants have travelled to the bustling hub on the banks of the Bosphorus only to wilt amid the deafening noise of a Turkish football stadium.

They lost twice to Galatasaray last season and now, over the river to the Asian side of the intercontinental Istanbul, Liverpool fell flat at the hands of Fenerbahce – thanks to two Englishmen and a friend-turned-foe in the dugout.

Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown, born in Bradford and Birmingham respectively, both scored for Fenerbahce before Vedat Muriqi scored a winner as caretaker manager Dirk Kuyt, once a cult hero at Anfield, recorded a win in his final game in the dugout.

He will soon be replaced by ex-Newcastle and 101-cap Turkey midfielder Emre Belozoglu but Kuyt will not be forgetting this evening in a hurry in front of a raucous, hostile crowd in the district of Kadikoy.

As for Liverpool, who jetted home straight after the game and were due to land around 2am English time, they and boss Andoni Iraola were just glad to get out of Turkey, probably with their ears still ringing.

It was a poor night for Liverpool as they went down 3-2 against Fenerbahce in Istanbul

Andoni Iraola's side let a second-half lead slip and there were some terrible errors

Archie Brown sunk to his knees in celebration at full-time as the home crowd erupted

Trey Nyoni had scored his first goal in professional football and then Alexander Isak headed home to put Liverpool 2-1 up two minutes after coming on as a substitute but they were undone by sloppy defensive errors.

That will give Iraola plenty to ponder in the coming weeks given his side have conceded nine goals in their last three European games, all to opposition that would not be counted as part of the continent’s best in LASK, Villarreal and now Fenerbahce.

Aside from a UEFA Super Cup triumph over Chelsea at the home of Besiktas in 2019, Liverpool have struggled in this country and their last Turkish delight came against Trabzonspor, who now employ a certain Mohamed Salah, back in 2010.

Fenerbahce and Kuyt celebrated a famous win – as did around 45,000 home fans who produced deafening whistles every time Liverpool had the ball.

It was a true attack on the senses and Iraola’s side felt it, with several passes going astray as Kuyt’s men had the best of the first-half action and were unlucky to go into the break level at 1-1.

Liverpool had gone ahead on 25 minutes through Nyoni’s first goal in professional football, when a header from English full back Brown fell straight into the path of the Reds midfielder, who charged on to the ball like he was Steven Gerrard.

He needed a deflection off defender Kojo Peprah Oppong but cared not a jot as his volley ended up beating former Manchester City man Ederson.

It continued a stellar season for 19-year-old Nyoni, who has had a fairytale week that included a first Premier League start, first professional goal and also talks over a bumper new contract. To say it would be deserved would be the understatement of the season.

Trey Nyoni opened the scoring for the Reds but his goal came in a losing effort

Alexander Isak headed Liverpool back in front after some terrible Fenerbahce defending

FENERBAHCE (4-3-3): Ederson 5; Semedo 5 (Muldur 75), Skriniar 6, Peprah 6, BROWN 8; Guendouzi 7, Kante 7, Yuksek 5; Greenwood 8 (Aydin 89), Lukaku 7 (Muriqi 63, 6), Kahveci 7 (Arturkoglu 75).

Subs not used: Cetin, Gunok, Efe Demir, Mercan, Elmaz, Nene, Mimovic.

Scorers: Greenwood 29, Brown 73, Muriqi 79.

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 4; Gomez 5 (Wirtz 66, 6), Jacquet 5, Van Dijk 4, Tsimikas 4 (Kerkez 76); Nyoni 8 (Koumas 85), Mac Allister 7; Munoz 5 (Isak 66, 6), Szoboszlai 5, Ngumoha 7 (Gakpo 67, 6); Barcola 5.

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Araujo, Chambers, McConnell, Danns.

Nyoni’s goal, in theory, should have helped Liverpool settle. As it was, it did anything but.

Fenerbahce came out roaring and hit the bar instantly through Irfan Can Kahveci. With the next attack, they were level, just four minutes after falling behind.

Just like Liverpool’s goal, the Turkish side needed a hefty deflection to help them. Greenwood took a free-kick from 25 yards, Jeremy Jacquet turned his back on it and foxed Alisson. Two Brazilian goalkeepers, two wicked deflections that neither could do anything about.

Alisson was the best away player on the pitch in that opening 45 minutes, thwarting Greenwood, the brute force of Romelu Lukaku and fellow former Premier League favourite N'Golo Kante, who is now 35 but still has the energy of the young whippersnapper we all knew and loved.

Iraola turned to his bench with a £285million triple-change and two of them combined just minutes later, Cody Gakpo crossing for Isak to head home his seventh of the season.

But just as when they went 1-0 ahead, Liverpool retreated and invited pressure. A Kante cross was not dealt with by Gakpo and Brown could ghost in at the back post to score.

Then, on 79 minutes, Muriqi thumped home a header to put Fenerbahce 3-2 up and on their way to a memorable night.

Liverpool, who would have taken a huge step towards qualification with a win here, still have work to do.

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

#1345. EA Sports FC 27 Best Young Players: Highest Potential Wonderkids in Career Mode

EA Sports FC 27 is out now and that means you can dive straight into Career Mode. Here, building a successful team requires plenty of planning and one of the most important aspects in that respect is laying the foundations for the future so that a lasting legacy can be achieved.

Indeed, uncovering and nurturing the best young talents can be highly satisfying, especially if you help a player go from unheralded hot prospect to a world-class football genius known the world over. Whether it is finding the next Lionel Messi or emulating Sir Alex Ferguson by 'winning with kids', there is a lot of excitement in looking to the future on the field.

To help you on your way to trophies and acclaim in the game, GIVEMESPORT brings you all the best young players aged 20 and younger in EA Sports FC 27.

The two best young strikers in EA Sports FC 27 are, without doubt, Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi and Real Madrid's Endrick. The pair each have a potential rating of 88 in the game, with Junior Kroupi's current rating marginally better than that of Endrick.

Two more intriguing and potentially affordable prospects are Italian wonderkid Francesco Camarda, who is on the books at AC Milan (known as Milano in FC 27), and German forward Alexander Staff, who plays for Bayer Leverkusen. At just 18 years of age in the game, their current rating is relatively low in the 60s, but they have a high ceiling in terms of potential.

💡 DID YOU KNOW? Endrick has been compared to Brazilian legends Ronaldo, Romario and Pele. However, the forward dismissed the comparisons, telling GQ in 2023: "Man, nobody is going to be Pele. He's the king of football."

Robin van Persie's son, Shaqueel van Persie, has been impressing for Feyenoord in the Eredivisie, and he has the potential to mature into one of the best strikers in FC 27, while one player who could have an immediate impact and also develop into a world-class star is Christian Kofane.

Seventeen-year-old Brian Madjo has shown his potential in the real world for Aston Villa. A physically imposing youngster, Madjo already possesses impressive strength and could mature into an effective target man.

Who will be taking Desire Doue's crown in 2026?

As has been the case in the real world and previous FC games, Lamine Yamal is already one of the best players, with a frightening current rating of 90, but his potential is set much higher at 95, meaning he is expected to reach heights only ever scaled by the likes of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, two of the greatest football players of all time, in this game series.

Chelsea winger Estevao and Real Madrid attacker Yan Diomande are the two midfield stars deemed closest to Yamal in terms of potential, with that pair each potentially reaching a rating of 90.

In central midfield, Paris Saint-Germain and France anchor Warren Zaire-Emery is the best young star, while the likes of Kennet Eichhorn, Lennart Karl, Nathan De Cat and Ayyoub Bouaddi are up there too, with potential ratings in the high 80s.

Two Moras - Rodrigo Mora at Roma and Mexico's wonderkid Gilberto Mora - are widely touted to be among the best CAMs in the sport in years to come. Konstantinos Karetsas has been impressive since moving to Borussia Dortmund in the summer and his value is underlined by the fact that he is in the running for the 2026 Golden Boy Award.

The most gifted young footballers on the planet have been ranked in order.

At 19 years of age, Pau Cubarsi is already a world champion with Spain and he has proven his worth as one of the best centre-backs in world football at Barcelona. He is, thus, the best young defender in EA Sports FC 27 by a distance with a 91 potential rating. Brighton's Luka Vuskovic is a close second according to the EA Sports FC 27 ratings wizards.

Feyenoord's Givairo Read and Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly are deemed the best full-backs in the game, with the pair boasting a potential rating of 88 and 87 respectively. Interestingly, however, Lewis-Skelly is also capable of playing in midfield, so it will be interesting to see where his best role is in the game.

A wonderkid defender to look out for is is Georgian left-back Saba Kharebashvili. Despite having a relatively low current rating, his growth potential is phenomenal. Similar talent profiles include Kaua Prates at Borussia Dortmund and Daniel Banjaqui at Benfica. Such players may be more accessible for a mid-ranking team to recruit.

Surprisingly, Barcelona's famed La Masia doesn't rank at the top of the best academies in football.

It will come as little surprise to seasoned EA Sports FC players to learn that Dennis Seimen is the best young goalkeeper prospect in the game. The German shotstopper has a current rating of 72 and a potential rating of 87, meaning he could develop into a player of similar stature to the likes of Mike Maignan or Alisson, two of the best goalkeepers in the world right now.

Seimen's compatriot Florian Hellstern also has a high potential rating of 86, which would place him in a similar mould to the likes of Joan Garcia or Diogo Costa. Outside of Seimen and Hellstern, it is worth keeping an eye on Simon Eriksson and Aaron Yaakobishvili.

#1344. Scott Parker's baptism of fire: West Ham fight back from three goals down to earn draw at Cardiff in new manager's first match in charge

Published: 18:32 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:18 EDT, 5 November 2026

Scott Parker's West Ham launched a thrilling comeback from three goals down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff in his first game in charge.

Jack Moylan’s first hat-trick in English football had Cardiff in cruise control at half-time and the travelling fans were furious in the away end.

But the Hammers – inspired by captain Jarrod Bowen – fought back in incredible fashion as Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman netted to secure a point for the new boss.

Parker was confirmed as Hammers manager on Wednesday morning – just 24 hours after Nuno Espirito Santo was sacked.

Nuno was axed after a run of poor performances and the club opted to bring in a familiar face, with Parker having made 129 appearances for them as a player between 2007-2011.

It was a tough watch for the former England midfielder initially as Moylan had Cardiff 3-0 ahead inside 39 minutes.

Scott Parker took charge of his first West Ham game after Nuno Espirito Santo's sacking

Max Kilman is seen scoring the dramatic equaliser to make it 3-3 against Cardiff

Moylan scored a hat-trick on his Republic of Ireland debut against Grenada in May, but this was his first club treble since scoring three for Shelbourne in May 2023.

The draw extends Cardiff’s unbeaten home league run to 10 games over the last two seasons, while West Ham occupy the final play-off place in eighth.

Nuno’s 13-month tenure had ended after the Hammers had won just twice in six matches and lost successive home games to Southampton and West Brom.

Taty Castellanos had hinted at better times ahead, forcing Nathan Trott into early action after Bowen’s effort had deflected to him.

But the Hammers were behind after Alex Robertson found Moylan in the 11th minute. Moylan advanced to find the top corner of Mads Hermansen’s net with a ferocious strike from 20 yards.

Hermansen tipped aside Calum Scanlon’s cross and Will Fish headed over as Cardiff probed. There was no reprieve for West Ham when Perry Ng curled a ball over a static defence after 36 minutes.

Moylan cleverly slowed down for Morato to bundle him over, a clear penalty.

Cardiff had missed their last two spot-kicks, but this time Moylan was entrusted with the responsibility and sent Hermansen the wrong way.

Angry Hammers fans responded with cries of ‘you’re not fit to wear the shirt’, and many of them appeared to be making a swift departure three minutes later.

Jarrod Bowen was a key man for the Hammers as they staged a remarkable recovery

Joel Bagan’s corner cleared Fish at the near post, but Moylan came in behind him to head home his sixth goal in five games, and his 10th of the season.

Parker sent on Mohamadou Kante and Joel Piroe for Soungoutou Magassa and Castellanos at half-time and there was instantly more conviction from the Hammers.

Bowen floated a delicious pass through after 58 minutes, and Mukasa lifted the ball over Trott and in off a post.

The deficit was reduced further seven minutes later when Piroe flicked on Bowen’s pass and Engels slid home his first Hammers goal.

Kante nearly toe poked the ball past Trott before Kilman touched home Bowen’s brilliant cross, and West Ham almost won it through substitutes Ezra Mayers and Tomas Soucek.

#1343. Observation of prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

The dynamics of isolated quantum systems following a sudden quench has a central role in many areas of material science, high-energy physics and quantum chemistry1,2,3,4. Such far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics—which features complex phenomena with implications for thermalization, non-equilibrium phase transitions and Floquet phase engineering5,6,7,8—is challenging to study numerically, in particular, in high-dimensional systems9,10. Here we use a programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator11 to systematically explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits. By initializing the system in a product state and performing quenches across a broad parameter space, we discover several stable, qualitatively distinct dynamical regimes. We trace their robustness to Floquet-like prethermal steady states8 that are stabilized over exponentially long emergent timescales by strong dynamical constraints. We further observe sharp peaks in the dynamical response that are quantitatively explained by the structured melting of prethermalization through resonances. In two dimensions, we uncover a prethermally driven, first-order dynamical phase transition linked to the proliferation of Néel-order defects6,12, and probe it quantitatively using a generalized Clausius–Clapeyron test. Together, these results establish a programmable route to high-energy prethermal phase structure: long-lived dynamical phases, their resonant breakdown and a first-order dynamical phase transition that is not inherited from the equilibrium phase boundaries.

Numerical simulations for a 1D chain of N = 16 atoms with periodic boundary conditions and Rb/a = 1.4. a,b. Simulations including the full experimentally relevant noise model. a. Time evolution of \(\langle {\hat{O}}_{ZZ}\rangle \) at Δ/Ω = 0.2 and 3.7. Solid curves show noisy numerics including readout confusion; shaded regions indicate the total 1σ uncertainty obtained by combining trajectory and shot-noise errors in quadrature. Noiseless numerics and experimental data are shown for comparison. b. Time-averaged \(\langle {\hat{O}}_{ZZ}\rangle \) versus detuning, averaged over 0≤t≤4 μs; shading indicates the corresponding total 1σ uncertainty. The noisy numerics use the Aquila-relevant noise model of Extended Data Table 1, with 20 stochastic trajectories, 120 shots per time point, and a sampling interval of 0.01 μs. c,d. Simulations including only positional atom disorder. c. Increase of the resonance peak width near Δ/Ω ≈ 3.7, relative to the zero-disorder case, as a function of the positional disorder strength σp, extracted from Lorentzian fits, together with a simple classical estimate. d. Time-averaged \(\langle {\hat{O}}_{ZZ}\rangle \) versus detuning for several values of σp. Increasing positional disorder selectively broadens and smooths the resonance peaks, while leaving the rest of the long-time response comparatively unchanged under experimentally relevant noise.

Experimental results for 180 atoms on the cut Rb/a = 1.4. a. The time-averaged expectation values of several k-island observables, namely the xyd 1-island observable and the xy k-island observable for k = 1, 2, 3, over time intervals with (top) different initial times ti and fixed final time tf = 4.0 μs, and (bottom) fixed initial time ti = 0.8 μs and different final times tf. The grey dashed vertical lines mark the quench parameters of the time series in panel b, namely the peaks of each island operator (Δ/Ω = 0.0, 1.2, 3.6, 4.8) and the point close to the right exit of the xy 1-island operator region (Δ/Ω = 2.0). b. The time evolution of the expectation values of the xyd 1-island observable and the xy k-island observable with k = 1, 2, 3. The drawing on the right shows an example of island conversion processes possible in the 2D system (equivalent to the 1D island conversion Hamiltonian discussed in the Supplementary Information). The arrows in the panels indicate the time series segments for the main resonance at Δ/Ω = 3.6 that tentatively reveal island conversion dynamics: two-islands are rapidly created and then slowly converted into a mix of one- and three-islands. The experimental data shown are derived from 100 samples per time evolution, with error bars denoting one standard deviation across the samples.

a. The time-averaged expectation values of the island operator sum on the cut Rb/a = 1.4 for 16 atoms, and the thermal expectation values of the observable for the effective temperature of the quench using the nearest-neighbor blockade subspace (thermal xy blockade) and the full Hilbert space (thermal full). b. The dependence of the time-averaged blockade violation density \({\hat{O}}_{nn}^{(1)}\) (also shown in Extended Data Fig. 6a) on V1/Ω at representative constant detuning cuts for 144 atoms. To normalize the blockade violation density to the connectivity and boundary conditions, we scale it by N/NB, where NB = 2NxNy − Nx − Ny is the number of nearest-neighbor bonds. The states along these cuts are prethermal, and thus over a fixed time interval the time averages after peak exhibit exponential scaling [equation (22)], as evidenced by the dashed lines showing fits \(\propto {e}^{-c({V}_{1}/\varOmega )}\). As shown in the Supplementary Information, the upward curvature observed in the experiments relative to the clean exponential scalings at large V1/Ω can be explained by the position disorder, while the calibrated readout errors set the final saturation floor. The experimental data shown are derived from 100 samples per time evolution, with error bars denoting one standard deviation across the samples.

a. The dependence of Δc/Ω (as extracted from \(\overline{\langle {\hat{O}}_{L}^{(1)}\rangle }\) using the procedure described in Methods) on inverse linear system size for Rb/a = 1.4 cut. The classical prediction, given by Δc/V2 = 2 − 2(1/Nx + 1/Ny) + 2/(NxNy), is shown for comparison. b. The dependence of the conjugate variable jump ratio (\({\delta }_{c}\overline{\langle {\sum }_{i}{\hat{n}}_{i}\rangle }/{\delta }_{c}\overline{\langle {\sum }_{i}{\hat{n}}_{i}{\hat{n}}_{\langle \langle i\rangle \rangle }\rangle }\)) on the inverse linear system size. The jump ratio is used to probe the Clausius-Clapeyron relation at the DPT. Both the transition point and the jump ratio converge as the system size increases, consistent with a first-order transition. The experimental data shown are derived from 100 samples per time evolution, with error bars denoting statistical and fitting uncertainties as described in Methods.

The classical spin dynamics model is described in the Supplementary Information, where the 2D square lattice has coordination numbers z1 = z2 = z3 = 4. a. Dynamical phase diagram in terms of the long-time averages of the (squared) spin component \({S}_{z}^{2}\). Panels b,c show the three (squared) spin components on b. the cut Rb/a = 1.4 across the phase transition and c. the cut Rb/a = 0.7 across the crossover, each indicated by a grey dashed horizontal line in panel a. The black dashed lines in panels a,b show the phase transition from the approximate analytic solution of the Stoner-Wohlfarth model.

Experimental phase diagrams extended down to Rb/a = 1.0 for 144 atoms. a. The time-averaged expectation values of the Rydberg density observable \({\hat{O}}_{n}\) and the k-neighbor correlation observables \({\hat{O}}_{nn}^{(k)}\) for k = 1, 2 (defined in the main text). Besides the crossover, at low Rb and Δ ≈ 2V1 we observe another distinct dynamical regime, which corresponds to antiblockade dynamics73 characterized by expanding excitation loops74. b. The time-averaged expectation values of the xyk-island observables \({\hat{O}}_{L}^{(k)}\) for k = 1, 2, 3 (equation (4) and surrounding text). The atom schematics in the upper corners show the types and sizes of Rydberg excitations that the observables measure. The grey horizontal line indicates the lower bound Rb/a = 1.2 of the phase diagrams for 180 atoms shown in Fig. 4a. The first-order DPT smooths to a crossover at low Rb, in analogy with the classical Stoner-Wohlfarth scenario (Extended Data Fig. 5). The experimental data shown are derived from 100 samples per time evolution, with error bars denoting one standard deviation across the samples.

The lattices are shown for Rb/a = 1.4. 1D lattice with a. 52 atoms; and b. 16 atoms, where the field of view can accommodate 2 parallel copies with separation b = 5a. 2D square lattice with c. 180 atoms; and d. 16 atoms, where the field of view can accommodate 6 parallel copies with separation b = 5a. e. Pulse sequences. (Top) The Rabi frequency Ω is set to a constant value Ω/2π = 2.5 MHz. (Bottom) The detuning Δ is set in the range Δ/Ω ∈ [−4.0, 6.0], and shown here for Δ/Ω = 0.4.

Experimental results on the cut Rb/a = 1.4. Panels a-c show experiments with (left) N = 52 atoms and (right) N = 16 atoms. The geometries are shown in Extended Data Fig. 7. a. The time-averaged expectation values of the \({\hat{O}}_{nn}\) observables and the k-island observables \({\hat{O}}_{L}^{(k)}\) for k = 1, 2, 3. Experimental \({\hat{O}}_{L}^{(k)}\) data is equivalent to Fig. 3b. b. The time evolution of the expectation value of the 1-island observable for several values of Δ/Ω on the right exit from the central region, shown as dotted vertical lines in a. c. The time-average \(\bar{p}(\alpha | \varDelta /\varOmega )=\frac{1}{T}{\sum }_{i}p(\alpha | \varDelta /\varOmega ,{t}_{i})\) of the Hamming weight probability distribution \(p(\alpha | \varDelta /\varOmega ,t)={\rm{Tr}}\,(\rho (t){\hat{P}}_{\alpha })\). Projectors \({\hat{P}}_{\alpha }\) arise from the spectral decomposition of the (unnormalized) Hamming weight operator \({\hat{Q}}_{n}\equiv N{\hat{O}}_{n}={\sum }_{\alpha }{\lambda }_{\alpha }{\hat{P}}_{\alpha }\), where λα = 0, …, N denote the possible Hamming weights. The time average is equivalent to marginalization over ti with p(ti) = 1/T. The grey dashed vertical lines identify the distribution at Δ/Ω = 0. d. The mean and variance of the time-averaged Hamming weight probability distribution at Δ/Ω = 0, measured in experiments with different system sizes N. The data are linear, with fits yielding the slope of ~0.275 ± 0.002 for the mean and ~0.106 ± 0.006 for the variance, shown respectively by the red and green solid lines. The approximate scalings are 1/4 and 1/8, shown respectively by the red and green dashed lines, consistent with a state that ergodically explores the blockade subspace. e. The time-averaged Hamming weight probability from numerical simulations with 16 atoms. The experimental data shown are derived from 120 samples per time evolution for 52 atom experiments and 100 samples per time evolution for 16 atom experiments, with error bars denoting one standard deviation across the samples.

Numerical studies of multiple observables, scaling, and averaging for the 1D chain in a circular geometry on the cut Rb/a = 1.4. The time-averaged expectation values are computed as \(\overline{\langle \hat{O}\rangle }=\frac{1}{{t}_{f}}{\int }_{0}^{{t}_{f}}{\rm{d}}t\langle \hat{O}(t)\rangle \). a. The time averages of the blockade-violation density \({\hat{O}}_{nn}\) operator, the diagonal \({\hat{O}}_{ZZ}\) operator (also presented in the main text Fig. 2d), and the off-diagonal \({\hat{O}}_{XX}\) operator. The \({\hat{O}}_{nn}\) response vanishes at the main peak, but captures the resonances, suggesting their origin from blockade violations; the \({\hat{O}}_{XX}\) response showcases non-analyticities at points where the dynamics is expected to change abruptly. b. The time averages for different system sizes N = 10, …, 20 and final time tf = 10 μs. The curves are nearly identical, indicating a weak system size dependence. c. The time averages for N = 16 atoms and different final times tf. The curves rapidly converge in tf ≈ 0.5 μs. The dashed line denotes the curve for tf = 100 μs, which is the longest time examined in the numerics, while the squares denote the diagonal ensemble averages, which are equal to the time averages in the strictly infinite-time limit. d. The time averages of the blockade-violation operator for N = 16 atoms and different quench parameters Δ/Ω, reflecting the 1D experiments in Fig. 3a. Similar to the experimental results, the curves show exponential decay, corroborating prethermal dynamics even at small system sizes.

Numerical results obtained using the time-evolving block decimation (TEBD) method for a chain of N = 52 Rydberg atoms with open boundary conditions. The blockade radius is Rb/a = 1.4. The system is evolved up to \({t}_{\max }=4.0\,\mu {\rm{s}}\) with a time step Δt = 0.01 μs, and the Hamiltonian includes nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor interactions, with longer-range terms truncated. a. Real-time dynamics of \(\langle {\hat{O}}_{ZZ}\rangle \) for two representative detunings, (top) Δ/Ω = 0.0 and (bottom) Δ/Ω = 0.5, illustrating convergence of the oscillatory behavior with increasing maximum MPS bond dimension \({\chi }_{\max }\). b. Time-averaged value \(\overline{\langle {\hat{O}}_{ZZ}\rangle }\) as a function of detuning Δ/Ω, where the plotted values are averaged over the final 2.0 μs of the evolution. The curves correspond to different maximum bond dimensions \({\chi }_{\max }\). Both the real-time dynamics and the time-averaged observables exhibit rapid convergence as \({\chi }_{\max }\) increases, with \({\chi }_{\max }\gtrsim 256\) yielding nearly indistinguishable results, indicating that the dynamics are well converged with respect to entanglement truncation at the probed times.

#1342. Four players earn first call-ups in latest Italy squad: Everything you need to know

Four players earned their first senior national team call-ups when Roberto Mancini announced his squad of 31 Italy players for November’s Nations League fixtures against France and Belgium, plus another who is set to earn their first ‘proper’ taste of international action: Here is everything you need to know about the fresh faces in the latest Azzurri squad.

Italy will be in action against France in San Siro next Thursday, November 12, and away against Belgium on Sunday, November 15.

As things stand, Italy sit in second place in their Nations League group on seven points after four matches. France lead the way on 10, Belgium are in third on six and Turkiye are bottom on zero.

Ahead of the November round of fixtures, Mancini announced a squad of 31 players on Thursday evening, which included first call-ups for 17-year-old Como midfielder Riccardo Cassano, Parma 18-year-old Simone Lontani, Milan top scorer Alphadjo Cisse and recent Champions League goalscorer Mattia Liberali.

There was also a call-up for Luca Koleosho, who earned his first two caps in a pair of friendlies under interim head coach Silvio Baldini back in June, as part of a squad that was made up almost entirely of players from the U21 squad. This is his first call-up to a competitive camp.

The most surprising inclusion on the list is 17-year-old Cassano, who has not yet made a competitive appearance at club level.

The talented teenager, who likes to play in front of the defence, capable of dictating and breaking up play, was only promoted to Como’s U21 squad at the beginning of the season and earned his first call-up to the U18s squad in September.

He travelled, trained and earned minutes with the senior Como side during pre-season, but is yet to appear competitively under Cesc Fabregas. His appearances this season have all come in the Primavera league or in the UEFA Youth League.

Cassano will spend the first few days of the international break with the senior Italy squad and will have an opportunity to impress in front of Mancini, but will then be released back to the Italy U18s squad, where he is more likely to earn match minutes this break.

Like Cassano, 18-year-old Parma forward Lontani will also spend the first few days of the international break with the senior Italy squad before returning to the Italy U19s to earn game time at the right age group.

The teenager, who came through the academies of Cesena and Milan, joined Parma over the summer and has gone on to score five goals from his first 11 senior appearances at club level, including three in 10 outings in Serie A.

Lontani’s appearances so far this season have largely come as a second striker, but he is capable of covering in a number of central positions as well as on the left wing if required.

It was only a matter of time before Cisse was included in the Italy squad: There had been calls for him to be included back in September as well. The 20-year-old, in his first season, is currently Milan’s leading goalscorer across all competitions with seven from 12 appearances.

He brings a level of versatility to the Italy attack, capable of playing as a striker, in a supporting role behind the centre-forward or as a left winger.

Unlike Cassano or Lontani, Cisse will be targeting his first minutes for the senior Italy side during the November round of fixtures.

Fresh off scoring his first Champions League goal in Como’s historic 9-1 drubbing of Lens earlier this week, Liberali will have an opportunity to prove his worth with the Italy squad this month.

The 19-year-old is not quite a regular in the Como line-up just yet, but is beginning to earn opportunities off the bench under Cesc Fabregas. He current has two goals and two assists from six appearances across all competitions so far this season, three of those goal

Involvements were in the 9-1 victory over Lens on Wednesday night.

He and Cisse know each other well given that they both spent the 2025-26 season in Serie B with Catanzaro.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1341. Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

The strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

The spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after big-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

All eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1340. Sir Alex Ferguson Named the Greatest Player in Premier League History

Rob is senior football editor at GiveMeSport, with over 15 years experience covering sport in various capacities since graduating from the University of Gloucestershire in 2008 with a degree in journalism. A childhood obsession for all things football developed into a career writing about the beautiful game, initially producing content for clients including Luton Town Football Club and the PGMOL. His first big interviews were with Premier League referees Howard Webb and Michael Oliver in 2009. He then spent four years producing written content for a betting website, mainly focusing on football, and was there to cover various games and tournaments including the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012. Rob joined GiveMeSport in 2013 (initially as a sub-editor before becoming a senior writer and then senior editor in 2020) and has covered countless football matches and other sporting events, interviewed various high-profile figures including Rio Ferdinand, Peter Crouch and Theo Walcott, and written well over 10,000 articles during that time. Rob has played a key role in GiveMeSport's coverage of the World Cups in 2014, 2018 and 2022, plus Euro 2016, Euro 2020 and Euro 2024, along with many Champions League finals. While football is Rob's area of expertise, he has also covered a wide range of other sports during his time at GiveMeSport including boxing, tennis and darts, as well as the 2016, 2020 and 2024 Olympic Games.

Sir Alex Ferguson, regarded by many as the greatest football manager of all time, once named the player he believes is the best in Premier League history.

Twenty-four former players have been inducted into the Premier League’s Hall of Fame since its creation in 2021.

The Premier League’s all-time leading goalscorer Alan Shearer and Arsenal legend Thierry Henry were the first two players inducted, followed by Roy Keane, Frank Lampard, Dennis Bergkamp, Steven Gerrard and David Beckham.

Others are certainties to be inducted, such as Cristiano Ronaldo, one of the greatest footballers in history, who scored 103 goals for Manchester United and won the Premier League Player of the Season award in 2007 and 2008.

Fellow shoe-ins include Mohamed Salah (193 Premier League goals) and Harry Kane (213 Premier League goals).

However, only players who are officially retired from professional football are eligible to be inducted into the Premier League’s Hall of Fame.

One player conspicuous by his absence is Ryan Giggs, winner of more Premier League titles (13) than any player in history.

Only James Milner (658) and Gareth Barry (653) made more Premier League appearances than Ryan Giggs (632), who also boasts the highest number of Premier League assists (162) by a distance.

No official explanation has been given for Giggs’ continued omission, although BBC Sport noted in January 2025 that many have concluded ‘the controversy over his character lay behind his absence’.

Asked by his former Manchester United teammate whether it plays on his mind, Giggs said: “Not really. No, I mean, I don't think about it until you just brought it up. I don't think about it. I think when you start off, you don't... These are the things that you're not striving for. You're striving off to win games and try and win trophies. That's the most important thing for me.”

There’s little doubt that Ferguson would have inducted Giggs into the Hall of Fame if it were down to him.

Ferguson named Giggs as one of only four genuinely world-class footballers he managed at Manchester United, and even labelled the Welshman as the best player in Premier League history back in 2009 - five years before Giggs retired aged 40.

"We have had a lot of top-class players in this league – and some have probably made more of an impact than Ryan – but nobody can boast the same sort of longevity and consistency," Ferguson said of Giggs, per The Guardian.

"He was there when the league started and he is still there now. I think you would have to say Ryan is the best."

While some lean towards the likes of Henry, Ronaldo or Shearer among the greatest Premier League players of all time, the greatest manager in Premier League history believes Giggs’ remarkable longevity and consistency puts him in pole position.

#1339. Spence included in England squad for the first time since €35m Inter transfer

Inter wing-back Djed Spence has been included in the England national team squad for November’s Nations League fixtures: His first call-up since completing his €35m transfer to the Nerazzurri over the summer.

Spence has been included in Thomas Tuchel’s 25-man squad for England’s upcoming Nations League fixtures against Croatia on Thursday, November 12 and Spain on Sunday, November 15. He is the only Serie A representative in the latest Three Lions squad.

This is Spence’s first call-up to the England side since the 2026 World Cup, where he helped his nation to the semi-final and an eventual third-place finish, and his first call-up since his €35m transfer from Tottenham to Inter over the summer.

It took a while for the 26-year-old to regain full fitness after an extended post-World Cup break: His first appearance for the Nerazzurri did not come until after the September-October international break, in a 3-0 Serie A win over Parma on October 10.

He is called back into the England squad despite the fact that he has made just one Serie A start after 10 rounds of fixtures so far this season. He has made six appearances across all competitions so far for Inter, three in Serie A and three in the Champions League for a total of 272 minutes.

#1338. Andoni Iraola blasts Liverpool stars for 'cheap and messy' defeat at Fenerbahce - and blames the NOISE inside stadium for second goal as Turkey curse continues

Published: 18:10 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:18 EDT, 5 November 2026

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola blasted his ‘cheap and messy’ side after they fell to a 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce.

Former cult hero Dirk Kuyt was in the dugout as two Englishmen – Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown – scored for the Turkish giants to cancel out Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak’s strikes before Vedat Muriqi headed home a winner.

All three goals were avoidable but may have been due to the deafening atmosphere and Iraola said: ‘(They were) cheap goals. Messy goals.

‘The free-kick is quite far out, through the wall. The last goal was a long throw, the second one Cody (Gakpo) touched the ball just in front of Alisson.

‘In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate, it was difficult for me to give instructions and the communication was difficult between Cody and Ali.’

Iraola also stressed his frustration with his team conceding three from set-pieces, saying: 'It's something that we were doing very well in the league, we were doing quite well until today.

'We knew it was one of the strengths of Fenerbahce. We concede from a free-kick, a corner and even from the long throw at the end.'

Tonight's loss was Liverpool's second in as many games but first in the Champions League this season

Vedat Muriqi's 79th minute header sealed the victory for Fenerbahce

Liverpool full-back Kostas Tsimikas also had some criticisms of the Reds defensive performance as he said: 'We didn't defend after the goal we conceded. After three or four minutes, automatically, we conceded another goal. I think we have to mark better if we want to win games.'

Meanwhile Kuyt, who played 285 times for the Reds, said: ‘It was a very special night for everyone who loves Fenerbahce. I have to give a very big compliment to the players and the staff who keep pushing them.

‘We told each other to stick together and be united. That’s something I learned from Liverpool, who we played against. We made a miracle tonight, not many expected us to win.’

It was Liverpool’s second straight defeat after the 1-0 reverse at home to Arsenal and the third Champions League game on the bounce where they have conceded three goals.

The result was also the third defeat in Istanbul in 13 months, extending Liverpool's miserable run in Turkey since their 2005 Champions League final heroics.

Iraola's side travel to Crystal Palace on Sunday.
