#1337. 25 Best Defenders in World Football Right Now (Ranked)

A strong defender is vitally important to any successful football team. Sorting out the back-line is crucial, and having some serious defensive talent is a surefire way to build a team destined for silverware. Much focus is placed on attacking players, which is why any list of the best footballers in the world will always be dominated by that type of star.

However, we've highlighted the best defenders in the world right now, in order to give them their flowers for a change. From buccaneering full-backs to commanding centre-halves, the beautiful game is laced with talented defenders in all shapes and sizes. Here are the best players who operate at the back in a role that has been unsung for too long.

Given that trying to separate those on the list is such a difficult task, a number of factors will be taken into consideration as to where they end up in the rankings. These include:

The imposing France international is a great example of the modern centre back: athletic, composed, and complete with impressive attributes that exceed his defensive capabilities. Dayot Upamecano built a formidable duo alongside Ibrahima Konaté at RB Leipzig, leading both to the French national team and transfers to elite European teams.

Upamecano has established himself as a key part of Bayern Munich's defensive setup, securing several league titles and domestic cup triumphs since his move in 2021. With France, Upamecano has featured regularly, winning the Nations League in 2021 and playing the entire 120 minutes of France's World Cup final loss to Argentina in 2022. In 2026, he was one of nine defenders to be nominated for the Ballon d'Or.

Luka Vuskovic has been a revelation since joining Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2026. The Croatian has been tipped for great things since a loan spell at Hamburg put him on the Seagulls' radar in the first place. Tottenham Hotspur still decided to sell up, however, cashing in for as much as £50m.

Known for his aerial ability, recovery pace and modern passing range, the young defender is already among the very best in his position. The future is certainly bright.

Marc Guehi has been a fine defender for a number of years now but has really established himself at the highest level over the past three seasons.

He performed well for England at Euro 2024, as they made it to the final of the tournament, losing to Spain. He then followed that up by captaining Crystal Palace to their first-ever major trophy, as they defeated Liverpool in the FA Cup final, before beating them again to win the Community Shield a few months later.

Guehi earned a big move to Manchester City in 2026 after a 2025 summer move to Liverpool fell through. The England man has since established himself at the heart of the defence, helping the club to win the FA Cup during the 2025/26 season.

Alphonso Davies has been one of the most exciting attacking fullbacks in football for some time now, really breaking into the Bayern Munich team during the 2019/20 season, in which he helped deliver a treble – made up of the Champions League, Bundesliga and the DFB-Pokal.

In total, he has seven league titles under his belt in Germany and has enjoyed a great deal of success with Bayern. The only issue has been fitness problems, as injuries have regularly interrupted his momentum in Munich. Davies will hope to keep himself fit if he wants to move higher up this list.

Riccardo Calafiori has quickly become one of the best defenders in the world. Swapping centre-back for a fullback role at Arsenal, the Italian has often provided a surprise goalscoring threat, combining his instinct inside one area with his defensive prowess in the other. He is among the most undroppable players under Mikel Arteta.

Injuries have threatened to delay his progress, but Calafiori still played a key role as Arsenal finally ended their wait for another Premier League title in the 2025/26 campaign.

While AC Milan are counting their lucky stars that they took a punt on Theo Hernandez’s signature in the summer of 2019, it’s his previous employers, Real Madrid, who will be kicking themselves for letting him go for such a paltry fee. Since moving from Spain to Italy, most fans would agree that Hernandez consistently ranks among the world's best defenders every season.

From Essien to Kaka, here are the 10 greatest players who have played for Real Madrid and AC Milan.

Quick enough to burst forward with ease, while his high IQ allows him to marshal the back line from the left-back berth, the Frenchman has every tool to play at the top level of the sport for the next decade or so. However, a recent move to Al-Hilal may make it difficult for him to keep his place in this list without regularly playing in Europe.

Marc Cucurella has undergone what many would consider to be somewhat of a redemption arc in the last couple of years. At Brighton, he was lauded as one of the best left-backs in the Premier League before his 2022 move to Chelsea led to a decline in form as he came close to being kicked out of Stamford Bridge within a year of his arrival.

What seemed to catapult him back into better form was Spain’s Euro 2024 victory. From that point, the full-back regained his confidence and mojo and, as a result, became an incredibly valuable member of both Chelsea and Spain's squads. After winning the 2026 World Cup with Spain, Cucurella earned a huge move to Real Madrid during the 2026 summer transfer window.

Over the course of the last 24 months, Willian Pacho has transitioned from a young defender looking to show his worth in European football to a winner of the continent’s biggest competition and one of its most highly touted defenders.

The Ecuadorian, who made a name for himself in Belgium and Germany before his big-money move to the French capital in 2024, has settled in at the Stade de France incredibly well. Linking up with the likes of veteran Marquinhos, he has excelled thus far as part of the back-to-back Champions League-winning squad. The future continues to look bright for Pacho.

When Abdukodir Khusanov's header allowed Chelsea to open the scoring just three minutes into his Manchester City debut, many predicted that it would be the defining moment of his Man City career for all the wrong reasons. Since then, however, he has been among the best defenders in the world.

The young centre-back is among the quickest in his position in the Premier League, if not the world, and uses that recovery pace to his advantage. Despite his age and relatively small stature, Khusanov also has no trouble when asked to outmatch opposition forwards on a physical level - winning 60% of his duels in the 2025/26 campaign.

There were some doubts over Ezri Konsa's ability to step up for a side like Arsenal. Those doubts couldn't have been put to bed any quicker if he tried, however.

The England defender has taken a seat at the top table and has not looked back since, having also won the Europa League with Aston Villa in the 2025/26 campaign. At the start of the 2026/27 season, he ensured that the Gunners didn't miss William Saliba during his absence for a single second.

It's worth noting that Konsa is also an England mainstay these days. The centre-back has earned his place for the Three Lions and could be crucial if they are to finally end their wai for silverware.

#1336. The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

This is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

There was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k

The midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

This is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

Instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

They are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

In the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other big signings to respond.

But this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. “It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, said. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

“You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”

This occasion, more than anything, is crying out for someone to play how the supporters are feeling and it’s not there yet. It’s been tame and Manchester City are, accordingly, comfortable.

City motor forward on the counter through Cherki, whose delightful touch takes him away from Mac Allister. From inside his own half, the Frenchman dribbles to the edge of Liverpool’s penalty area. He attempts to play a one-two with Fernandez, but the pass is cut out by Jacquet.

Manchester City have not got going, as of yet. The defiant message from the club is they would not let the verdict affect them. They have defended well enough but have barely strung a passing sequence together against a Liverpool side who appear be playing off pure emotion.

Gravenberch is bossing this game in midfield. Another powerful run from deep results in a delightful nutmeg on Fernandez, who slips over. Liverpool’s energy has been really impressive. City need to ride out this early storm.

It’s getting heated at Anfield! Mac Allister and Anderson clash sparking a scuffle between both sets of players. It threatened to boil over for a second, but the drama quickly calms down and play resumes after the referee has a word with the two captains.

All fairly difficult to stomach, the Manchester City fans’ performance at kick-off. Inflatable bananas to signify nostalgia for the late 1980s, when these were all the rage after the club’s relegation to Division Two? The City of Sheikh Mansour are about as far removed from the era of Jimmy Frizzell as is possible to imagine, with their colossal wealth enabling cheating on an unprecedented scale. And as for the Poznan during You’ll Never Walk Alone? When Liam Gallagher asks Oasis fans to perform this backwards dance during next year’s tour, I suspect there will not be quite the same take-up.

There’s an early flashpoint as Koumas puts Guehi under serious pressure, causing the defender to fall to the ground and grab the ball with his hands. It’s not a foul and Liverpool are given a free kick. The hosts want Guehi booked and Araujo sprints over to the referee waving an imaginary yellow card, but gets one himself.

Amid all the build-up and backstory to this extraordinary fixture it is remarkable that 21-year-old Lewis Koumas is making his first Premier League start as Liverpool’s makeshift centre-forward. And he has started well.

A spell of Man City possession has slightly quelled the atmosphere. On paper, you would have to say the away side’s starting 11 is superior to Liverpool’s.

Liverpool make a fast start as Gravenberch effortlessly turns Fernandez and Munoz darts inside of O’Reilly. The winger’s shot is smothered by Guehi, but the early signs are encouraging for the hosts.

City get us under way at Anfield. This is one we’ve quite literally all been waiting for.

A roaring rendition of YNWA is bellowed by Anfield, which is in full voice. City players huddle together and go over to clap their fans in a show of solidarity.

In the corner of the stadium, where the Sir Kenny Dalglish Stand meets The Kop, there is a white banner with black paint proclaiming: “A generation of supporters cheated” - none of this is bothering the Manchester City fans, who are going back a generation and have a raft of inflatable bananas. (It was a craze in the 1980s, for you younger readers). Anyway, let’s get on with the game and what an opportunity this is for young Lewis Koumas, who has produced the individual performance of the season so far for Liverpool against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup. He needs to be a scampering, scurrying menace once again.

The Kop has now started a chant of “you cheating b-------” you know what you are. Doubt it will be the last time we hear that this afternoon. They are now singing “going down, going down, going down”.

No chance of hearing the names of the Manchester City players as the team is read out by the PA announcer. He is drowned out by the boos, jeers and whistles from the Liverpool fans. The atmosphere is certainly starting to build.

A re-imagining of Oasis’ Wonderwall at the front of the Kop. “And after all,” the banner reads, “you really robbed us all.”

Andoni Iraola told Sky Sports: “He came back from the international break with an overload. He felt a tight hamstring.

“He tried somehow pushing through training, but he was not feeling 100 per cent.

With just over 15 minutes until kick-off, here’s a recap of the two sides.

Liverpool: Alisson, Araujo, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez, Gravenberch, Mac Allister, Barcola, Wirtz, Munoz, Koumas.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Gomez, Endo, Chiesa, Tsimikas, Frimpong, Nyoni, McConnell, Ngumoha.

Man City: Donnarumma, Matheus Luiz, Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly, Anderson, Fernandez, Semenyo, Cherki, Ndiaye, Haaland.

Subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Doku, Vitor Reis, Gvardiol, Bouaddi, Allan, Khusanov, Lewis.

When asked if the mindset and mood are right for him to do his job, the City boss replied: “Yes. Absolutely. Yes.

“The mood is good, the mindset is good. Now it’s time to start the game - finally!

“It [togetherness] is very important; the mix between the players and the fans, everyone.

“We are away in a complicated environment, a complicated stadium, but we are going to do our best to try to win the game.”

The Manchester City players are out for their warm-up and, dare it be said, they were greeted with apathy by the Liverpool fans. Not even the murmur of a boo when Erling Haaland and Co emerged. It surely will be very different when kick off comes.

The current City players found themselves in a peculiar situation as none of this is their fault, but they’ll be the ones who receive the brunt of abuse from rival fans as the public-facing figures of the club. They’ll need to be braced for a hostile reception at every away ground in England.

However, you can expect Anfield to turn up the heat to one of the highest levels, given how alleged City’s actions have impacted Liverpool’s trophy haul.

Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool finished second in the 2018-19 season, accumulating a staggering 98 points, while winning 30 matches and losing just once. City incredibly pipped them to the Premier League trophy by one point. A strikingly similar scenario occurred in the 2021-22 campaign, with Liverpool placing as runners-up with 92 points. You guessed it, City had 93.

What’s done is done, and ultimately we are entering a territory of ifs, buts and maybes. However, if City’s appeal against the charges is unsuccessful and the guilty verdict is upheld, then Liverpool would have unfairly missed out on historic success and lifelong memories.

The current City players found themselves in a peculiar situation as none of this is their fault, but they’ll be the ones who receive the brunt of abuse from rival fans as the public-facing figures of the club. They’ll need to be braced for a hostile reception at every away ground in England. However, you can expect Anfield to turn up the heat to one of the highest levels, given the aforementioned landscape and how City’s actions have impacted Liverpool’s trophy haul.

In turns out that the two City buses arrived in a different entrance, round the back of Anfield Road. This was a clever tactic in avoiding the ferocious build-up of revved up Liverpool fans.

Manchester City bus arrived without any issue, came into Anfield on a different route and into the stadium with a police escort. Let's all try to concentrate on the game now. https://t.co/ybe1I27LSi

Liverpool bus has arrived to a scene of billowing red smoke and the thousands who have gathered singing “Allez Allez Allez!”

No sign of City bus, and the fact that police have now reopened Anfield Road from the Prince Harry pub towards the stadium suggests there may not be one at all. Several silver and black minivans with blacked-out windows arrived a few minutes ago – were the Manchester City players inside them?

The Liverpool fans have just started singing: “Going down! Going down! Going down!” and it’s incredible to think this could be the last meeting at Anfield between the sides for the foreseeable future.

This was the meeting in English football for the last decade and the quality was never higher than between 2018 and 2022. Over those four seasons, Manchester City amassed 358 points. Liverpool’s total was 357. Incredible how one team ended up with three titles and the other only had one.

The Police operation is in full swing. Drones are flying low up and down Anfield Road and the number of high visibility jackets has increased in the last five minutes. The songs are varying between praise for Liverpool players – Alexis Mac Allister is currently in vogue – and scorn for Manchester City. Definitely more people here now.

Around 30 minutes before the buses are expected to meander down Anfield Road and, already, vantage points are being taken and throats are being cleared. For scale, there isn’t the same volume of people (yet) as there has been for title run-ins and European nights but there is going to be a crackle in the air soon enough.

“You cheating b------s, you know what you are” is audible already.

The Opta supercomputer has spoken, awarding City a 40.7 per cent chance of winning this afternoon against Liverpool’s 34.6 per cent.

However Maresca’s men well know that conqueroring Anfield is one of football’s toughest tests. In fact, away teams have only won 12.5 per cent of all Premier League matches at Liverpool’s storied home.

“Should have made it a sham and pineapple,” the company’s official account comments.

News breaks that City had been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.

Telegraph Sport understands that Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur were contacted in advance of the email to the other 15 clubs.

In a letter to fans, a defiant Khaldoon Al Mubarak, City’s chairman, expresses complete confidence that his club would be vindicated.

“There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club,” he writes. “We will not give them that opportunity.”

With the football world still making sense of the news, Tony Pulis admits to feeling “cheated”. His Stoke City side were defeated by Manchester City in the 2011 FA Cup final, during the 2009-23 period.

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali then likens City’s transgressions to “doping” before Mauricio Pochettino, whose Spurs side were often in the hunt with City for major trophies during his time as manager, says that football has “lived through a period of deception”.

The Premier League reveals that City’s owners inflated “sham” sponsorship deals by £830.69m between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

It also discloses that image rights had been inflated and key witnesses had lied.

Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group, appears helpless when questioned about the verdict’s findings at the European Football Clubs’ general assembly in Copenhagen by Sky News.

An unblinking Soriano then features in a video statement published by City in which he claimed their guilty verdict was based on “a single false accusation”.

With City on the ropes, Pep Guardiola releases a statement in support of his former club, assuring supporters that “we will get through this together”.

The Prime Minister says that he would be “really concerned” to lose City’s owners, but after significant backlash, No 10 moves to clarify his reaction saying that “if wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences”.

It later amends the statement to “wherever wrongdoing is established”.

The UAE then warns Andy Burnham that it will pull billions of pounds of investment out of the UK in retaliation for the guilty verdict against City.

City argue that their sponsorship deals were part-funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club’s owners, in their appeal, which claims bank statements and witness accounts provide “irrefutable evidence” to support their case.

The Liverpool head coach was asked for his reaction to City’s guilty verdict in his pre-match press conference and, as with many of his peers, he kept his response brief.

“Uncertainty is not good for anyone involved,” he said. “But there is the process ongoing and we have to be patient like everyone else and see what happens at the end.”

It is the most unlikely Oasis song title for a banner but, in a sea of canvas, the word will jump out from the Kop: Acquiesce.

The simplest flags frequently carry the most profound messages and, on a red background, below Acquiesce is the declaration: “MCFC Cheats”. It has been prepared specially and specifically for the return of domestic football to Anfield.

Given the tone coming out of the Etihad Stadium, nobody will be acquiescing to any alleged wrongdoing, certainly not on Sunday, but minds were made up on Merseyside about how far City had pushed the boundaries in pursuit of success a long time ago.

“There has been a lot of talk about various things,” explains John Gibbons, host of Anfield Wrap, the popular Liverpool podcast. “Manchester City trying to say they are going to be hard done to, but there are no great surprises among Liverpool fans about these charges, are there?

“Everyone who goes to the match, who supports Liverpool, have known all along that a lot of those sponsorship deals looked questionable. Did they pass the smell test? That’s why the atmospheres in the past when City came were always brilliant and I’m expecting it will be the same again.”

So that is why Anfield will be a maelstrom of sound and fury for one of the most significant occasions in Premier League history.

The half-and-half scarves have been replaced by more topical match-day merchandise this afternoon...

Here is what City’s head coach said during his first press conference after the guilty verdict:

“There is a process ongoing and in this moment I completely trust the club … I trust the club because I trust the people and this is also the reason why I joined the club. And then there is not another club in the world where I would [rather] be.”

“Absolutely not. The last time I was here was the treble season. I know the effort from the players, from the club, from the manager in that time that was Pep [Guardiola]. I know exactly the effort that the club put to achieve that kind of target.”

“I won the Championship with Leicester. League One, we will see, but we are thinking about something that we don’t know.”

I’m not worried at all. The environment [among] the players is nice. In this moment we are top of the league so the players have all the reason to be happy and excited.

“One hundred per cent… Because I know the organisation from years ago, and I know how serious they are, I know that they do the right things. I would like to speak about this when we win the appeal.”

While Liverpool have struggled for wins in this fixture of late, it’s worth noting that this run includes five draws.

On Saturday Manchester United fans resurrected their “ticker” mocking Manchester City’s trophy drought following their rivals’ cheating scandal:

There was also a nod to Rui Pinto, the whistleblower whose Football Leaks documents prompted the Premier League’s investigation into City:

There were four days between the news leaking that Manchester City had been found guilty of the majority of charges first levelled at them by the Premier League in February 2023 and the independent commission findings dropping.

Staff, then, had had a bit of time to process a guilty verdict although little, it seems, could adequately prepare them for the excoriating tone and content of the commission’s ruling.

“The thing that has shocked me more than anything is the language the commission used to describe the club’s conduct,” one staff member told Telegraph Sport this week.

“We had been waiting for a very long time to see what came out of these Premier League charges and lots of different things go through your head. But I just wasn’t expecting that. I’m still a bit shell-shocked by the ferocity of what the commission said. I think that’s what’s worried me.”

"Enjoy the ride and smile" Erling Haaland with a message for Man City fans ahead of their trip to Anfield this weekend 🎙️🩵 https://t.co/H7so0fk6XE

“The international break is good because we can review what we have done and what we can do better,” Enzo Maresca said after Manchester City’s harum-scarum 5-3 victory over Sunderland. “But at the same time we can relax a little bit more.” One wonders how much respite Enzo Maresca and Manchester City actually enjoyed in the intervening 21 days.

Since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. Until then, though, the show goes on and City’s players and staff must compete knowing that their every move now comes with a caveat.

City have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca said, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

Given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

#1335. In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1,2,3,4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5,6,7,8,9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1–SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

a, Quantification of CD3− cells 5 days after CRISPR-mediated gene editing in three independent donors. b, Quantification of live cells 5 days after editing with the indicated Cas9 mRNA concentrations, n = 3 biologically independent replicates. Data are shown as mean + s.e.m. Significance was calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test. ns, not significant. c, Left, representative flow cytometry plots showing CD3 and CD28 protein-level DKO efficiency in activated human primary T cells 5 days after Cas9 mRNA electroporation. Right, quantification of CD3+ CD28+ cells in DKO and vector control groups; data are shown as mean + s.e.m.; n = 4 infection replicates. Significance was calculated using a paired two-sided t-test, ****P < 0.0001. d, Quantification of CD3− or CD28− cells 5 days after editing; n = 3 donors per concentration. Data are shown as mean ± s.e.m. e, Classification and composition of targeted genes in the T cell DKO CRISPR library. f, Schematic of the two-step T cell DKO CRISPR library construction process. g, Quantification of plasmid library sgRNA-pair construct distribution. h, Flow cytometry histograms showing EGFRvIII expression in U87-GL and U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell lines. i, Flow cytometry histograms showing PD-L1 expression in U87-GL and U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell lines. j, Schematic of DKO CAR-T cell library generation pipeline, including human T cell isolation and activation, CAR-T cell generation and selection, lentiviral DKO CRISPR library infection and Cas9 mRNA electroporation. Schematic in panel j created in BioRender; Chen, S. https://biorender.com/4g9xapi (2026). k, Spider plots of tumour volumes for donor 1 in vivo screen experiment shown in Fig. 1d. n = 5 biologically independent mice. l, Representative H&E-stained tumour sections from two biologically independent tumours per group from the screen shown in Fig. 1c. Scale bar, 250 μm. m, sgRNA-pair detection rates from the total library across individual samples. D, donor; T, tumour. n, Heat map of Spearman correlation coefficients between the log2-normalized counts-per-million (log-norm.) sgRNA counts for each sample. Data were arranged by hierarchical clustering using the ward.D2 method. o, Multidimensional scaling analysis of log2-normalized screen data using the top 10,000 most variable sgRNA pairs across samples. Data points were clustered by k-means. p, Box-dot plot of library representation across individual samples, showing the distribution of all sgRNA-pair constructs counts. Boxes indicate the 25th–75th percentiles, center lines indicate medians, and whiskers extend to the most extreme values within 1.5 times the interquartile range. Individual points represent sgRNA-pair counts. q, Empirical cumulative distribution function of DKO library representation among detected sgRNA pairs in plasmid, pre-injection cell and tumour samples. Sample labels in m-p indicate sample type, plasmid, pre-injection cell or tumour, and donor ID.

a, Distribution of the top four performing sgRNA-pair constructs for top DKO hits across samples, ranked by SAMBA sgRNA z-score. b, Heat map of DKO screen scores for all pairwise gene combinations assessed in the CRISPR screen. Values were scaled and visualized within a range of −1 to 1. Hierarchical clustering was performed using the Ward.D2 method based on Euclidean distances. c, Scatter plot showing the relationship between screen enrichment and synergistic effect. SAMBA z-scores were plotted against synergy scores for each gene pair. Dashed lines indicate FDR-adjusted P value, q < 0.05, for epistasis and SAMBA results. d, Scatter plot of observed DKO SAMBA scores versus expected SAMBA scores based on the additive effects of the corresponding SKOs for each gene pair (SKO1 + SKO2). Points are colored by synergy score. Linear regression yielded R2 = 0.0152 (n = 2,485 gene pairs; 71 SKO genes), indicating minimal predictability of DKO outcomes from SKO additivity. e, Quantification of indel frequencies in DKO-edited CAR-T cells 5 days after electroporation across three independent batches. P values were calculated using unpaired two-sided t-tests. Data are mean ± s.e.m.; n = 3 human donors. Each dot represents one human donor. f, Quantification of indel frequencies in CAR-T cells from three donors generated across three independent batches 90 days after gene editing. P values were calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC. Data are mean + s.e.m.; n = 3 independent donor-derived CAR-T cell preparations, generated from three donors in independent batches. NS, not significant, *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001.

a, Quantification of live cells 5 days after editing in different DKO CAR-T cells compared with controls, n = 3 infection replicates per group. b, Schematic of generation of DKO CAR-T or CAR-Jurkat cell generation and downstream assays. Schematic in panel b created in BioRender; Chen, S. https://biorender.com/7vyyd1r (2026). c, Quantification of Ca2+ flux AUC and peak signal change in different DKO CAR-Jurkat samples. The resting region was defined as 1 min before antigen crosslinking, and the peak region was defined as 500 s after cross-linking. AUC is calculated as (mean peak signal – mean resting signal) × 500. E:T = 1:2. n = 3 per group per time point. f, Schematic of the NFAT/AP-1 GFP reporter structure and quantification of GFP+ cells. g, Schematic of the NF-κB CFP reporter structure and the quantification of CFP+ cells. h, Quantifications of tonic signaling in CAR-Jurkat cells after 1 month cell culture without stimulation, n = 3. P value was determined by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s correction for multiple comparisons test versus GTC. i, Left, representative flow cytometry histograms showing CD107a expression in CD8+ DKO and GTC CAR-T cells after 2-h coculture with U87-GL-EGFRvIII cells. Right, quantification of CD27+ DKO CAR-T cells after two rounds of tumour stimulation on day 5; n = 6 per group. For each round of coculture, E:T = 1:4. o, Quantifications of LAG-3, PD-1, and TIM-3 expression in CAR-T cells after repeated tumour challenge on day 5, n = 4 per group. For each round of coculture, E:T = 1:4. p, Quantification of LAG-3+, PD-1+, TIM-3+ CAR-T cells after two rounds of tumour stimulation on day 5; n = 4 per group. For each round of coculture, E:T = 1:4. q, SPICE analysis of LAG-3, PD-1, and TIM-3 expression in CAR-T cells on day 5. Data in d-g,k right,m,r are mean ± s.e.m.; data in a,h-j,k left,l,n-p are mean + s.e.m. Dashed lines in c, i, j, n-p indicate mean values of the GTC group. n indicates biologically independent samples unless otherwise stated. a, Schematic of the time-series RNA-seq experiment in DKO, NR4A1 SKO, SOCS3 SKO, and GTC CAR-T cells undergoing repeated tumour challenges. b, Principal components analysis (PCA) of all RNA-seq samples across all stimulation time-points (left) or separated by timepoint (right). #1334. Thomas Tuchel Reveals How Close Dewsbury-Hall Came to England Call-Up

Sam C is a sports journalist with a growing reputation for producing insightful and engaging multimedia football content. With a background in presenting and digital storytelling, he has contributed to a range of high-profile platforms, including The United Stand and Sky Sports, where his work has reached millions across YouTube and social media.

Educated in media and journalism, Sam blends strong editorial judgement with a clear understanding of online audiences, specialising in content that covers Premier League football, transfer news, tactical analysis and fan culture. He is particularly known for his coverage of Manchester United, where he delivers breaking news, interviews, and in-depth features with a sharp eye for detail and accuracy.

His experience spans live presenting, video production, and article-based reporting, all of which are underpinned by a commitment to quality journalism and digital impact.

You can also find his work on platforms such as The United Stand: https://www.youtube.com/@UnitedStand

England manager Thomas Tuchel has revealed that Everton midfielder Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall came extremely close to earning his first senior international call-up, praising his performances and explaining where he sees the 28-year-old fitting into his system.

Dewsbury-Hall has enjoyed an impressive spell at Everton, establishing himself as an important player and continuing to push for international recognition.

Despite his performances, the former Chelsea and Leicester City midfielder was left out of Tuchel’s latest England squad for the upcoming internationals against Croatia and Spain.

His Everton teammate James Garner, however, was included once again, raising questions about how far Dewsbury-Hall remains from receiving his first senior opportunity.

Speaking at Wembley on Friday, Tuchel was asked by GIVEMESPORT reporter Sam Cohen about Dewsbury-Hall’s omission, particularly given his performances for Everton and previous involvement in England’s provisional squads.

The German was full of praise for the midfielder and admitted that he had been seriously considered for selection.

“Very good player, very good season, you can just see it,” Tuchel said.

“He’s a very good football player overall because I see him in the way we play now.

“I don’t see him in central midfield in the build-up and in the build-up of the game. I see him more in the finishing part of the game as an offensive eight or almost as a 10.”

Tuchel’s assessment offers an interesting insight into how England’s coaching staff view Dewsbury-Hall’s qualities.

Rather than considering him primarily as a deeper midfielder responsible for progressing possession, the England boss believes his strengths are better suited to operating further forward, where he can influence attacks in the final third.

However, that is also an area of the pitch where England have considerable competition for places.

“The competition is very, very high in our squad in this position,” Tuchel continued.

“But he is, as you know, he’s in our 55, a standout player for Everton and we see his quality.

He’s a nice watch because he’s a very, very good football player and was very, very close for me.

Those comments will offer encouragement to Dewsbury-Hall, who has previously spoken about being included in England’s provisional squads without making the final selection.

While Garner’s inclusion demonstrates that Tuchel is keeping a close eye on Everton, Dewsbury-Hall faces a different challenge because of the attacking midfield role the England manager believes suits him best.

Crucially, Tuchel’s comments suggest the midfielder is not being overlooked entirely.

Instead, he remains firmly within England’s wider selection picture, with his performances at club level continuing to attract attention.

For Dewsbury-Hall, the task now is to maintain his form and convince Tuchel that he deserves an opportunity in one of the most competitive areas of the England squad.

Grealish will NOT be involved in Everton’s next Premier League fixture either.

#1333. Como talent Ramon included in Spain national team squad for the first time

21-year-old Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon has earned his first ever call up to the senior Spain national team squad for Nations League fixtures against Czechia and England coming up in November.

Ramon is the only Serie A representative in Luis De La Fuente’s latest Spain national team squad ahead of Nations League fixtures against Czechia on Thursday, November 12 and England on Sunday, November 15.

The Real Madrid academy product earns his first national team call-up after an excellent start to the 2026-27 season with Como, where he has played almost every minute across the first 14 competitive matches of the campaign. He has only come off before the 90th minute on two occasions so far.

He has also proved a handful from set-pieces with three goals and two assists to his name after 14 matches at club level in 2026-27. He netted his first Champions League goal in a 4-1 victory over Manchester United earlier this month and was also part of the side that claimed an historic 9-1 win over Lens earlier this week.

It is a case of one in, one out for Serie A players in the Spain national team squad: Ramon is called in, but Inter goalkeeper Josep Martinez drops out after earning his first call-up last month.

Goalkeepers: Unai Simon (Athletic Club), David Raya (Arsenal), Joan Garcia (Barcelona), Alvaro Valles (Real Betis).

Defenders: Marc Cucurella (Real Madrid), Alex Grimaldo (Atletico Madrid), Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona), Aymeric Laporte (Athletic Club), Marc Pubill (Atletico Madrid), Pedro Porro (Tottenham), Dean Huijsen (Real Madrid), Jacobo Ramon (Como).

Midfielders: Martin Zubimendi (Arsenal), Pedri (Barcelona), Mikel Merino (Arsenal), Fabian Ruiz (PSG), Alex Baena (Atletico Madrid), Fermin Lopez (Barcelona), Pablo Barrios (Atletico Madrid), Marco Roca (Real Betis).

Forwards: Nico Williams (Athletic Club), Lamine Yamal (Barcelona), Ferran Torres (Barcelona), Mikel Oyarzabal (Real Sociedad), Yeremy Pino (Crystal Palace), Ander Barrenetxea (Real Sociedad), Roberto Fernandez (Espanyol).

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1332. Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR

It should have been three. Again Wissa was partly to blame, losing the ball in midfield to set Coventry on the counter-attack. When Botman made a mess of a clearance it spun perfectly into the path of Cherif. The net should have bulged but the £20m summer signing from Fenerbahce scuffed wide.

The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE

In a flash the balance of play shifted in Newcastle’s favour. They poured forward in search of the equaliser. Jaissle switched to a 4-4-2 with Will Osula joining Fernandez-Pardo up front, but instead of pulling level, Coventry pulled further ahead.

"We need to improve the things we can control, and right now that's a lot" 🗣️ Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle expresses his disappointment after his side's loss to Coventry 👇 https://t.co/fatJkZYyRM

Very, very satisfying. It’s so hard to win. We played like the team we want to be here. A team you look at and go there’s so much energy and spirit in the group. We know we are going to have to suffer this season, when we don’t have a lot of the ball. We have to understand it. The level is what it is.

The work ethic, the belief. You get what you deserve. Great finishes. We haven’t quite had the rub of the green this season and that might have helped us nick a couple of more points. I’m a firm believer that you keep going. It was a complete performance. We’ve got to keep our feet on the ground because we’re going to have to do 30+ of those but it’s a great feeling for the players.

[Cherif] is very, very exciting because he is so young. He has got a really good manner. He wants to train, he wants to learn. He’s quite quiet but on the pitch he shows a lot of personality. When you see the quality of the strike and the hold-up play, there’s a lot to come from him.

"That one was for you, nan" Jack Rudoni explains his goal celebration ❤️ https://t.co/79OvHMlu6J

A victory to savour for Coventry whose teenagers Cherif and Mfuni scored fine goals. No doubt they wobbled when Botman equalised and for the next 10 minutes but Newcastle blew too many chances and resumed making errors at the back. Newcastle’s squad is a mess.

Newcastle might maintain that Thomas-Asante was offside and blocking the keeper’s view when Mfuni pulled the trigger but I think Hornicke had a clear view and hence it wasn’t an offence.

The first two minutes of stoppage time, of which there are four, pass without incident.

Osula lifts a volley over the bar with a wild attempt. Toure was injured in the build-up and will be replaced by Dan Burn.

Never mind Bob Gelodof and Brenda Ann Spencer, Matthias Jaissle doesn’t like Mondays. They are 8-2 down on Monday Night Football so far this season.

Coventry 4 Newcastle 1 (Mfuni) The substitute had only just replaced Rudoni and took the ball on the inside-left 25 yards out, advanced then wrapped his instep around a left-foot shot, arrowing it across Hornicek into the bottom right.

Stephen Mfuni makes his mark for Coventry! 👊 https://t.co/KI2kgpfUJP

Thomas-Asante crashes a right-foot shot into the heart of the left post. A thumping strike that leaves the metalwork ringing.

Coventry 3 Newcastle 1 (Simms) Right foot shot from 18 yards through Thiaw’s legs, clipping the inside of his right knee to deflect it into the bottom left. Joelinton had been trying to dribble it out of the box, overhit it and fouled Thomas-Asante as he tried to recover. The whistle was betweeen the ref’s lips but he did not exhale as Simms steered his shot through Thiaw’s legs.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

Touré beats Dasilva for pace down the right then blazes over from a tight angle then moments later is given an opportunity to shoot and sticks it in the stands again. Both times the cross was on.

Toure has caused untold problems for Dasilva. Newcastle corner on the left is bent far too deep and goes out for a goal-kick.

Wissa dithers over a shot when found by Toure to the right of the penalty spot and finally clips it into Thomas. Coventry are clinging on but flapping. As is the crowd.

Hall, following Botman’s lead, lets fly from distance, straight at Rushworth.

Coventry fluff a couple of chances to break with hasty, panicked passes.

It was as if Coventry were defying him to have a shot. And in doing so, the nerves are back with a bang in the crowd.

Coventry 2 Newcastle 1 (Botman) Coventry invite him to shoot by backing off and backing off and he RSVPs with a left-foot torpedo from 20 yards into the roof of the net. What a strike!

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE

Barnes appears to have been brought down by Sakamoto in the Coventry penalty area but he was offside. One of Jaissle’s staff is booked for some verbal transgression.

Joelinto rattles bones in a tackle that was not shown as they focus on Barnes’ spurious penalty appeal when he slipped behind Pinnock.

Rudoni dips his shoulder and skins Botman in the Newcastle box but tries and fails to square it to Cherif instead of shooting.

Touré makes ground down the right and slips Joelinton down the inside. The substitute, who took the captain’s armband off Thiaw, tries to find Pardo with a cross that Thomas blocks.

Now Willock blazes over from eight yards on the right after a slick one-two with Murphy.

Dedic → MileyTouré → MurphyJoelinton → Willock

Rushworth drops Hall’s cross but recovers to grab it on the bounce. Jaissle has three subs stripped. Murphy tries to bend a cross from the right to Barnes at the back post but Van Ewijk and Thomas combine to scramble it out for a throw-in.

Now Cherif misses a gilded opportunity after a hacked clearance from Botman lands at his feet to the left of the spot. He kicks it into his other leg and the ball dribbles wide. The way Botman dealt with Thomas-Asante’s cross was really shoddy.

Barnes disguises his inside run and evades Van Ewijk to collect Thiaw’s pass up the inside-right channel. He spins and feeds it infield to Wissa who telegraphs his shot with a laboured touch before swiinging a right-footer from 25 yards straight down Rushworth’s throat.

Newcastle have been awful. Seem to lack leadership and heft on the field. The return of Joelinton can’t come quick enough.

Coventry 2 Newcastle 0 (Cherif) Talented lad. Absolutely larrups a right-foot shot through a thicket of Newcastle legs from 18 yards when a long throw was headed out to the edge of the box.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR

Collison between Van Ewijk and Willock leaves them both winded and needing treatment. The Newcastle midfielder had been trying to bullock down the middle in purusit of a pass.

Coventry overload with seven men on the right before rolling the kick-off to the left-footed Rushworth who launches it too far up that wing and Hornicek gathers.

Interesting half for Matias Fernandez-Pardo who has been in the middle of most of Newcastle’s best moments but has failed to take two excellent chances.

The first was baffling as the Belgium international made no attempt to sweep in Jacob Murphy’s cutback at the near post, letting it run through his legs thinking Harvey Barnes was in a better position. He wasn’t.

The second was a little unfortunate as he did well to time his run and wriggle free of centre back Bobby Thomas. That put him in on goal with just the goalkeeper to beat, but having sat Chris Rushworth down he pushed the ball a fraction too wide and by the time he was in a position to shoot, Thomas had done brilliantly to cut off the angle and block it.

Coventry have been good but Newcastle have been really poor again away from home. They are yet to put a 90-minute performance together since the opening weekend against Liverpool. Matthias Jaissle will want a lot more from his team in the second half.

Newcastle should at least be level given their chances but you have to admire Coventry’s spirit and work rate. Cherif seems to me to have a high ceiling and at 19 is already a real handful.

Newcastle need to stop fannying around and buy a proper centre-forward. Wissa is better wide or in a more fluid system, as I suspect Fernandez-Pardo is, too. Stick Osula on and get the chequebook out in January. Offer Boro £50m for Lankshear.

Cheeif, working his socks off, chases a lost cause and retrieves a long pass forward in the whitewash but when he turns to try to play it to Thomas-Asante, Thiaw makes a good tackle.

Hall turns away Mason-Clark’s effort from the left and the game turns into a basketball match… without the scoring as both sides fly from end to end.  Two minutes of stoppage time to come.

Thomas to the rescue again, He was outpaced by Fernandez-Pardo running on to straight ball down the middle but kept on going when the Belgium forward rounded the keeper to block the shot. Fernandez-Pardo may have been better off taking on the shot earlier, surprising the advancing Rushworth, rather than trying to take him out of the equation. Or dinked it before he got too close.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. #1331. Viktor Gyokeres shows he still has an important part to play for Arsenal after starring role in win over Slavia Prague as Mikel Arteta begins next phase of his masterplan, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 17:03 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:19 EDT, 5 November 2026

The next phase of Mikel Arteta’s season masterplan was seemingly underway: get the Arsenal frontline firing.

The plaudits for a defence which has conceded just eight goals across the Premier League and Champions League are well endorsed.

Yet, as Viktor Gyokeres was making a compelling case for challenging Kai Havertz’s spot, Arteta’s backline decided to have a temporary, rare malfunction.

By full-time Slavia Prague’s winless streak in the Champions League had reached 23 games — the joint-worst ever in the competition alongside AEK Athens, despite a late onslaught which momentarily caused the visitors jitters. Slavia boosted their shot count up to 17, compared to Arsenal’s 12. The north London club had taken their eye off the ball having reached half-time two goals up.

David Raya was called upon for a world-class save, using his full frame to dive and deflect Oskar Kubiak’s header onto a post.

Wiktor Nowak then pulled a goal back on 90 minutes from inside the area having collected substitute David Jurasek’s pass to tap home near the goalline.

Noni Madueke celebrates scoring the opener for Arsenal against Slavia Prague

Viktor Gyokeres netted the second for the Gunners with this curling effort

Nowak had another chance, as he went agonisingly close to a further Jurasek cross. Such laxness by Arsenal would be punished elsewhere in Europe, though they still remain unbeaten in the Champions League after four matches.

An annoyed Arteta said: ‘It was two very different halves. The first one, where we played at a really high level. It should have been three, four or five (goals).

‘Right from the beginning (of the second half), we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we had to do, in every concept.

‘I already mentioned a few things and some others that I will keep to myself.’

Even without William Saliba, who made the squad for the first time this season following a back injury sustained at the World Cup in July, the Gunners have usually been imperious in defence.

It’s their attack which has its fair share of holes, not helped by Bukayo Saka’s thigh injury and the lack of an in-form No9.

Yet, a bit of love and persistence can do wonders for a striker — and could be the antidote Arteta needs to rejuvenate Gyokeres, who caused Slavia a migraine with both his footwork and finishing.

Behind the Bane mask Gyokeres figuratively wears in his celebrations lies a man whose confidence has taken more than a knock or two.

Mikel Arteta made six changes to the Arsenal side that beat Liverpool at the weekend

Having struck 21 goals across all competitions last season, the Swede has largely occupied the bench in the current campaign.

Yet, the two pieces of play Gyokeres executed on a chilly Prague evening showcased just why he has an important part to play this season for Arsenal.

David Raya’s aerial punt accidently found its way to Gyokeres, following a defensive mishap, which the striker chested down.

SLAVIA PRAGUE (4-2-3-1): Domchak 5; Vlcek 6, Holes 6, Zima 6, Kubiak 5; Moses 6, Sadilek 6; Ayaosi 5, Sulieman 5, Sturm 5; Nowak 7.

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 7; White 6, Konsa 6, Gabriel 6, Hincapie 6; Zubimendi 6, Rice 7; Madueke 7, Merino 7, Eze 7; Gyokeres 8.

Instead of recycling the ball — an easier option for a man still finding his way — he went for the maverick option, producing a well-executed flick-on which found Noni Madueke. The winger reached the area, fending a defender off, before coolly slotting home.

Then before the break, Gyokeres had a goal of his own. After a neat one-two with Declan Rice, the Swede stormed into the box, before curling the ball in off the post from inside the area.

For all his deficiencies and limited chances thus far, the moment felt important for a striker who has now struck two goals and three assists in his past five appearances.

Havertz is Arteta’s No1, but one striker won’t be enough to properly sustain a campaign by which the league title and a first Champions League trophy in the club’s history are viable aims.

Even Madueke, enjoying a prolonged run on the right wing in Saka’s absence, was in inspired form.

Arteta made six changes to the Arsenal side that beat Liverpool at the weekend, with Merino earning a start on the ground where he exactly one year ago struck a second-half brace in Arsenal’s 3-0 victory against Slavia Prague last November.

Daniel Toula scored late on for Slavia Prague but they were unable to find an equaliser

Merino had his shot tipped over the bar after Madueke’s opener, the pressure already being felt by the home side.

Eberechi Eze went on a jinking run, featuring a nutmeg to the delight of the visiting fans, and it was all getting rather open.

The Gunners were close to going three goals up, Gabriel’s effort cleared off the line after Nazar Domchak spilled the ball.

Slavia suddenly came to life in the final minutes and had Arteta fretting on the touchline. An extraordinary turnaround was in sight.

Nevertheless, the form of Gyokeres will be a positive Arteta can take from a night not at his usual standards.

#1329. De Laurentiis arrives for Napoli crisis talks as Allegri faces growing scrutiny

Napoli owner Aurelio De Laurentiis has recently arrived at Napoli’s training ground for a series of crisis talks with head coach Massimiliano Allegri, his staff and players after a troubling period that has seen the team lose seven of their first 14 matches of the 2026-27 season.

Napoli have recorded back-to-back defeats over the course of the last week, away against Juventus and then a 4-1 hammering away against Porto in the Champions League.

This means that Allegri has now lost seven of his first 14 matches in charge of Napoli, leaving them in eighth place in the Serie A table and already 14 points off the league leaders after 10 games of the season. They find themselves in 27th place in the Champions League table with three points after four matches and are currently at risk of missing out on qualification for the knock-out rounds.

To make matters worse after the Porto loss, Matteo Politano painted a damning image of the state of the Napoli dressing room when he accused some of his senior teammates of not taking enough accountability, Kevin De Bruyne and Lorenzo Lucca were seen rowing with each other on the pitch and newspapers the following morning criticised a ‘divided’ squad that is supposedly breaking out into cliques.

Their next opportunity to redeem themselves will not be a particularly easy encounter either: At home against the Serie A leaders, Lazio, who have won all five of their away league matches so far this season.

The Napoli squad arrived for training on Friday morning and will remain together until their game against Lazio on Sunday.

Club President De Laurentiis has recently arrived at the training ground, according to reports from Gianluca Di Marzio, and will speak to the team and their head coach as he tries to get to the bottom of the current crisis.

#1328. Man City are not a team in Enzo Maresca's ideal image yet - their imperfections are clear as win at Leipzig shows they're learning on the job, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 17:30 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EDT, 5 November 2026

Watching Manchester City is not exactly straightforward at the moment. Downright confusing most of the time. Different tweaks on the same tactical theme each week, City learning on the job under new management.

Enzo Maresca recently revealed that he would rather win games 1-0 than these helter-skelter, drama-filled, error-strewn goal fests but they are not yet capable of producing that. And the players know it.

On leading in Saxony, secured by Castello Lukeba's own goal, Maresca called for Phil Foden and Abdukodir Khusanov to sprint for the bench to receive detailed instructions. As they did, Marc Guehi and Enzo Fernandez engaged in deep conversation. Gesturing arms as Erling Haaland and Elliot Anderson spoke while walking back to halfway.

The body language was as if they had gone behind. Strangely, that might encourage the boss. They know this all can improve drastically in a quest to become more cohesive. There is definitely the talent among the squad to possess a certainty of how to emphatically dominate games like this one.

None of this is particularly different to when they went on the seven-game winning run to fly out of the blocks in the Premier League, imperfections making them eminently watchable but not a team in Maresca's ideal image yet. Not by a long shot.

Later, when Anderson and Rayan Cherki were locked in debate about how to press from a goal kick, it served as a reminder of Maresca's words that this is a fresh project and change takes time. Chinks exist.

Erling Haaland came to Manchester City's rescue once more with the winning goal at Leipzig

He slid home City's winner with minutes remaining after fine work from Elliot Anderson (left)

Yet on the surface this presentable a creditable result, won by Haaland with 12 minutes left as they nestle inside the Champions League's top eight. All good for now, although added confusion comes in how little this could all mean amid an appeal of the independent commission's findings. Nobody is dissecting Maresca's evolving masterplan if they lose in court.

'We need to step up,' said Haaland, captain for the night. 'Keeping the ball, knowing when to keep it and when to go, working together offensively and defensively.'

Maresca himself admitted to shaking up the midfield and back four because he is feeling out a best XI, one he can rely upon and one that mixes that quintessentially City dominance and a more direct attacking line that can punish in a nanosecond.

'I need to understand more things about the players,' he said. 'That's why I'm so confident because I'm sure that we're going to be better and better.'

Coached by one of the Italian's closest friends and former City centre-half Martin Demichelis, Leipzig felt they deserved more. They went behind in unfortunate circumstances, although Enzo Fernandez lurked at the back post to do the honours from Nico O'Reilly's drilled cross had Lukeba not completed the job for him.

And Gianluigi Donnarumma was offering encouragement, almost embarrassed by Antonio Nusa's shot squirting through his fingers. Among other opportunities, Christoph Baumgartner curled wide from the box's edge. Baumgartner had oceans to himself amid a vacant City midfield. Anderson had gone to put out a fire out wide, vacating his holding position.

Anderson was operating there alone on the night, not something he has done regularly since a £116million summer switch, and it presented yet another iteration of Maresca's City as he attempts to locate the perfect formula.

Then two minutes summing up Donnarumma. Full stretch to acrobatically tip another Baumgartner shot wide seconds after the restart. And yet, shortly after, suffering one of those moments that are becoming far too common.

In an entertaining game, City took the lead initially when Castello Lukeba scored an own goal

Ridle Baku (right) equalised for Leipzig just after half-time due to a Gianluigi Donnarumma error

Enzo Fernandez restored City's lead with this emphatic header after Iliman Ndiaye's cross

Antonio Nusa saw Leipzig equalise for a second time before Haaland decided the game late on

RB Leipzig (4-2-3-1): Vandevoordt 6; Baku 7 (Henrichs 74, 6), Orban 6, Lukeba 4, Raum 6; El Aynaoui 6 (Seiwald 74, 6), Baumgartner 7 (Nkunku 57, 6), Banzuzi 6; Gruda 7, Romulo 6 (Gomis 67, 6), Nusa 7 (Reitz 73, 6)

Man City (4-1-4-1): Donnarumma 5; Nunes 6 (Dias 79), Khusanov 6, Guehi 6, O'Reilly 6; Anderson 8 (Bouaddi 83); Foden 6 (Doku 64, 6), Fernandez 6 (Kovacic 83), Cherki 7, Ndiaye 7 (Allan 83); Haaland 7

Ridle Baku was the beneficiary of the goalkeeper's poor positioning, forgetting about his near post, and flashed in. Somebody of Donnarumma's standing cannot allow that to happen. He would soon fumble another Baku shot, which led to a penalty appeal.

'It is not a concern but it is a mistake,' Maresca said. 'Before that he did a save that no other keeper in the world makes. Gigio knows he was not good with the goal. He's going to do better.'

City missed plenty of chances themselves before Fernandez headed in a second from Iliman Ndiaye's whipped cross but that lead only lasted three minutes, Nusa slamming into the far corner just after the hour. 'Silly goals,' Maresca said.

City kept ploughing forward, Anderson kept driving on. Ndiaye set Anderson storming down the right and he knew the area to hit. Back post, Haaland. A wicked cross, a striker's finish. Game won. Maybe that's what they were chatting about earlier.

#1327. Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

A fine team move ended with an excellent Stanway finish. It was her fifth goal in this qualifying campaign and she is England’s top scorer for 2025-26.

Tonight’s hosts are yet to qualify for a major tournament and are expected to set up in a defensive shape. England defender Esme Morgan believes the squad are ready for a long night of breaking down a stubborn opposition.

She told a pre-match press conference: “It’s just about persistence and trying not to get drawn into being frustrated by the opposition. A really good example was the away game against Ukraine in qualifying. We couldn’t seem to break through in the first half - the keeper was making saves, we hit the woodwork - but the messaging at half-time was just to keep continuing because we were creating opportunities.

”Not to start snatching or taking shots from distance, just trusting in our style of play and our ability to find gaps. We came out for the second half and scored really quickly. It’s just about sticking to the plan and being patient.”

Erica Meg Parkinson, one of England’s new midfielders, was apparently named after Eric Cantona.

While Cantona still famously is proud of his kung fu kick, when he attacked an obnoxious Crystal Palace fan, Parkison is less enthused by football’s most famous case of breaking the fourth wall.

“My dad is a huge Man United fan so I was named after Eric Cantona,” Parkinson says. “It’s a pretty good player to be named after except for, you know, the karate kicks.

“My brother was named after Denis Law. I don’t think my mum had much of a say in the name so she was dragged into it, but it kind of worked out because we both play football now.”
